reviews.text:
Lovely restaurant, relaxed atmosphere, delicious food and great friendly service from our servers especially Mandy. Thank you very much for your warm friendly service.
There were more dishes but everyone tucked into the food before photos were taken. Every dish was an amazing flavour.

We've been there twice, one for lunch, and one for dinner. Both times we came out happy.

The food is Levantine/Turkish, some with a twist. Last time we went there was for lunch, where you can combine a small plate and two salads for 21. We got two of these (i.e., 2 small plates and 4 salads), which is a decent amount for two people. We also got the hummus and a bread basket.

The hummus is good, smooth, like it should be (none of that grainy stuff). The pitta bread is great, but not a huge fan of the other types of bread. Next time I will stick with the pitta. The others didn't taste that flavorful.

For the small plates, we got the grilled chicken and the meatballs. The meatballs are tender, and both were well seasoned and cooked just right. The charred chicken skin was delicious.

For the salads, we got the aubergine, squash, tabbouleh, and califlower. They were all really good, but a bit on the colder side (as in, colder than room temperature).

Service is fast and attentive. I would go there again.

HIGHLY recommend this restaurant!
We had a great time in this restaurant. Food is super delicious and staff are so lovely and welcoming. Service was amazing and they don’t come and bother you every few minutes which is very rare in London restaurants.
We tried different salads which all were amazing. I really recommend Lamb Meatballs, very tasty. Prices are reasonable too for delicious food and great vibes!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Absolutely amazing experience at Amber!

We celebrated our end-of-year dinner at Amber, and it truly couldn’t have been more perfect. The food was so good — every dish was beautifully presented, packed with flavour, and clearly made with care.

The vibe was incredible too: warm, stylish, and full of great energy. It set the perfect mood for our celebration, and you could feel how happy and excited everyone was throughout the night.

A huge shout-out to the service team — the servers were attentive, thoughtful, and really paid attention to all the little details. They made the whole evening feel smooth and special from start to finish.

If you’re looking for amazing food, fantastic atmosphere, and top-tier service, Amber is an easy five stars. We left with full hearts and full stomachs — can’t wait to go back!
Great breakfast /brunch! The service is impeccable. Our Waiter James took great care of us - we had our 8months old with us and the high chair was spotless. We’ll come back to try dinner!

We had an amazing meal at Fare in Old Street! The tiramisu was heavenly, the croquettes were crispy and flavorful, and our mains were absolutely delicious. Everything was beautifully presented and full of taste, a real treat for the senses. The whole experience made for a perfect dining outing, and we can’t wait to come back!

My new wife Jess and I can’t thank FARE enough for making our wedding reception so special.

Florence thought of everything and ensured that the day was planned with meticulous timing. On the day, Joe ensured that everything ran on time and smoothly, and he couldn’t have done any more to ensure we were very well looked after.

All of the staff on the day did a great job of keeping all glasses topped up and drinks flowing. The food was 10/10 and we’re still getting messages saying the food was the best wedding food they’ve ever had!

The wine room looked incredible - it was the perfect intimate place to have our meal. The changeover from meal to dancefloor was seamless, and the brass band for the party in the wine room afterwards made it feel like an underground jazz bar - exactly the vibe we were hoping for!

Thanks so much to all of the staff (both front and back of house!) who made our wedding day so incredibly special and memorable. We would highly recommend FARE if you are looking for a cool reception venue in the city. Josh & Jess Clark
Delicious Mediterranean food with beautiful ingredients at the heart of Old Street. Grilled chicken with salad and dressing was very filling. Great service. Amazing tiramisu dessert.

We hosted our wedding reception with Fare in September and couldn't recommend the venue and team enough! We did a full venue hire and hosted a standing reception rolling into the evening event.

We were so incredibly happy with every detail of the day. The lovely Fare team were so helpful to our set up team, everything was on time and spectacular and we had such amazing feedback from our guests on every part of the day. The food and drinks at every part of the event were incredible (and kept coming!) from sharing platters and bowl food to late night pizzas. We danced the night away and had the time of our lives.

Huge thanks again for everything! We'll definitely pop in to see you all soon!

Sophie & Ian x

I arrived at Fare expecting a round pizza. A simple, predictable disc. Instead, they brought me this... this enormous, folded, tomato-bleeding leather pouch. It looked like a giant’s lost slipper.

My colleagues laughed. "You’ll never finish that," they whispered, as if I hadn't spent years training for this very moment. Poor fools.

I attacked the Calzone like a man with a grudge. Prosciutto, mushrooms, cheese—everything tucked inside like a delicious secret. It was a breeze. In fact, it was so easy I had to jump over and finish my colleague's Quattro Formaggi just to feel something.

My stomach was 90% dough, I could barely move, and I’ve never been happier. Top marks.

Good variety of food even for vegetarian. Really liked the starters and dessert. Red thai curry in mains can be more tasteful. But desserts were outstanding specially carmalised brioche. Melt in mouth, buttery, crispy outside.

Here briefly from the U.S First experience at a fine dining establishment like this. Lee was super attentive and made us feel comfortable even  while seated outside the heat lamps and the sun were perfect for the cold weather we aren’t used to enduring. I had pork Shnitzel my daughter had pizza my sister and her husband had red bean curry and roasted chicken everything was exceptional. The food the drinks the atmosphere the service everything was extraordinary. Lee gave us great new spots to try for the evening hopefully we come back soon to take advantage of all his recommendations. 10/10 for everything my expectations were beyond satisfied. Will definitely return.

The breakfast was amazing. Fresh and full of flavour. The staff were lovely. And I would absolutely get the Jalapeño corn bread again. As I was eating I was planning my next trip. Loved the environment, the location and the food.

I arrived very early for dinner with friends and the staff could not have been more welcoming and accommodating.
The evening atmosphere at Caravan is lovely as there are candles on the tables and in the windows which create a real sense of warmth and comfort. I LOVE all their seating outside as well with the blankets and warm sheep skins to sit on. Very Christmassy!

Popped in on a Saturday at 4pm to have a hot drink.

Service was polite and speedy.

Ordered the turmeric, lemon and ginger tea and flourless chocolate cake.

Very fresh and tasty.

Would highly recommend.
Had a 5pm dinner last night after the theatre - lobster and steak (valentines special) and service and food were excellent !!! Would recommend it as we’ve been a few times and it’s always great

Food was really good! However, the service was not great. We had a reservation at 8pm for 10 people, unfortunately 4 people cancelled last minute so we ended up being just 6. 3 of us were there at 8o clock and 3 arrived at 8:15. Around 8:10, someone that seemed like the manager or person in charge, asked us if we were ordering food and if the rest of the people were coming, we told him they were arriving in a minute and he proceeded to be incredibly rude saying that the kitchen closed at 8:30pm (online it’s said the kitchen was open until 10pm, I wouldn’t have made a reservation for 8pm if the kitchen was closing at 8:30) and if we didn’t order now we wouldn’t be able to eat, I told him that we had just arrived and he asked “wasn’t your reservation at 8? It’s 8:15! You need or order now!” I was honestly SHOCKED at the way he spoke to us. My friend told him we were going to wait for the other 3 people and in less than 2minutes they were there. We ordered our food in the next 10min and they served us. The food was good, but honestly I was there celebrating my birthday with my friends and being spoke to that way was incredibly rude and unnecessary. If your kitchen closes at 8:30 you should let people know about the right kitchen closing time, especially if you’re accepting a dinner reservation at 8pm, and it being a cocktail bar we were having some drinks first and we’re talking with no rush.
I understand that sometimes information online is not the same as reality, but you don’t have to be rude or miss treat people to get your point across, he could have just told us about the kitchen on arrival or just by having a different attitude.

Great little cocktail bar with a really nice vibe. The drinks were well made and the staff were friendly and attentive. The atmosphere was relaxed but lively, perfect for catching up with friends or going on a date. Would definitely come back to try more cocktails!

I have been coming to the drift for years and it never disappoints! Duck & waffle and Sushisamba get all the attention being on the top floor of the building, but people forget about this hidden gem on the ground floor! Food is always delicious, service is always great and the music & vibes are excellent.
I took my best friend for bottomless brunch and we loved it. I really liked that they had bottomless aperol spritz as an option. The service was great and they even gave us a complimentary dessert with “Congratulations” written on it because we were celebrating my friend’s engagement.
We stayed after brunch for extra drinks in the bar area and Gustavo made sure we were looked after, recommending loads of lovely cocktails to us!
I will definitely be back, and I’d highly recommend The Drift for your next lunch, brunch, dinner or /special occasion!

Our server Moni was so wonderful! It was my first bottomless brunch where I didn’t have to look around for a drink! The staff were so attentive, the food was great and the music , atmosphere so fab!!!!!x

Been here twice so far. The service was a bit slow but it was always filled with people on both the occasions. Tapas style portions so it was bit pricey for that but the food was really nice.

I tried the truffle pasta or Tagliolini al Tartufo the first time and it was really good - not sure if it was worth the price tag though.

Had the burrata ravioli in tomato sauce or Ravioli con Burrata e Salsa di Datterini this time and it was pretty good. I'd the pasta and the focaccia this time and still felt hungry after and I paid more than 20 GBP so the place is def pricey.

Popped into Lina Stores at the Bloomberg Arcade and it was a really lovely experience overall. The vibe is exactly what you would expect from the City, stylish and buzzing, though it did get quite noisy. With the after work crowd and some rather boisterous bankers nearby, having a proper catch up was a bit of a challenge, but the energy of the place is undeniable.

The food itself was very good overall, particularly the pasta which was beautifully cooked and managed to feel light rather than heavy. The Pici alla Norcina was the absolute star for me. That Umbrian sausage is incredibly delicious and creates a rich, hearty sauce that feels like a warm hug. I also really enjoyed the Pappardelle al Ragù di Osso Buco. The meat was wonderfully soft and the ragu sauce had a fantastic depth of flavour.

The Linguine con Granchio e Limone, which was pleasant but perhaps a little too subtle. At this price point, I was expecting a bit more punch from the lemon and certainly a more generous helping of crab, as the seafood felt a bit lost in the dish. However, the meal started and ended on incredible highs. The focaccia is fantastic with a really well developed flavour in the dough, and you simply must try the Torta al Cioccolato. It is easily one of the best ones I've had in a while, served warm and surprisingly light rather than dense. It was a complete joy to eat.

In terms of value, the prices feel a little steep for the portion sizes. I usually associate Italian dining with big, hearty portions, but these felt more tailored to the local City worker budget. It won't necessarily break the bank, but it is worth noting if you are coming in from further afield with a massive appetite.

The staff and service were absolutely fantastic and I really could not fault them. They were attentive and friendly despite how busy the room was. If you are looking for top quality pasta and a vibrant atmosphere, I would definitely recommend a visit, just perhaps not for a quiet first date!

What a wonderful, cosy place with delicious food! We came here for dinner based on the great reviews and it was a great choice! The atmosphere was cosy and welcoming, the lady who looked after us gave us a great advice on wine and made sure we were looked after. We are definitely coming back 😊

From the service, to the atmosphere, to the food prices, and the food everything was fabulous. We ordered a variety of dishes including the crab and lemon pasta, the short rib pasta, and the lemon chicken. Everything was great. Some shared a bottle of wine, with great selection, and others had a meter to sours, though limited liquor menu. We shared the chocolate mousse and tiramisu for dessert. Prices were reasonable and portions were plenty. Highly recommend if you’re in the area. But, suggest getting a reservation in advance!

Really fantastic pasta for the price. Great flavours, it was fresh. Portion sizes are decent and aesthetically the restaurants themselves are beautiful to sit in. Service was great as was the atmosphere, would definitely go back to this one, have been to the one in SoHo before and the pasta wasn’t as good.

Such a beautiful setting for an amazing meal! I am in the financial district of London for meetings and happened to find a local spot doing Sunday Roast...and they are doing it perfectly. The location is incredible (it is actually in the Royal Exchange building), the staff were so courteous and professional and the food - outstanding. I would highly recommend reservations. I was solo and even had fo wait (not long but make note). I am going back later this week for cocktails in the bar area. This is a must do.

Food was delicious and atmosphere nice as it was such a cute and chic location. Whilst the manager was great and very helpful and supportive of dietary requirements (gluten and dairy free) offering better options, the waitress was dreadful. I waited 45mins for a glass of champagne that came during my mains (hadn’t wanted it after that wait) and it was obviously forgotten as our other drinks came prior even though they took a while. I asked for the bill as we needed to leave to be somewhere else for another reservation, she stood next to the till chatting to other staff and my partner then asked for the bill 10mins later and she immediately went back and got it, obviously forgotten that too. Wouldn’t go back

I visited the restaurant for my late birthday celebration. Portion sizes were massive. We had burger and fish and chips. The burger was juicy and full of flavor. The fish and chips were not dry. Prices are reasonable too for this setting. I wasn't expecting for them to treat my dessert, it was very thoughtful. Thank you.

We were slightly nervous when we first walked into the bar, at it was pretty busy and loud - but were glad to hear that the restaurant was in a separate section that was much quieter, but also had a great vibe to it. The food was incredible and great value, they made personalised cocktails to our liking, and our server Ailish was incredible. She had great energy, provided incredible service and made the evening more special. Thank you :)

An interesting experience in a cool vault location. We had booked a table in the bar but upon arrival the door person seemed surprised that we had booked and told us to sit anywhere. It was surprisingly busy for a Monday. No table service so we ordered cocktails at the bar and had to explain a couple that were not part of their recommended menu. Drinks were tasty and made well but little friendly or positive vibe from the staff, merely a functional job done. Our group had a good time but that would be in spite of a very average customer service experience. Kitchen shut at 9pm FYI as we had hoped to get some small plates at the bar but were denied!

Great quality thai food. The service was amazing too, staff were very friendly and accommodating! I had the classic pad thai and it was amazing. Also we ordered a mixture of desserts - all delicious! Would recommend and will visit again!

Thai O’CHA Restaurant on Brick Lane is a real gem for Thai food lovers. The moment you step in, you’re welcomed with a warm and inviting atmosphere that sets the tone for a great meal. The menu offers a wide range of authentic Thai dishes, full of fresh ingredients and bold, balanced flavours. From fragrant curries to perfectly cooked noodles, each dish feels like it’s been prepared with real care and attention.

Being a huge fan of Thai cuisine, I can say Thai O’CHA is up there with my favourites. The food is consistently delicious, portions are generous, and the service is friendly and attentive without being overbearing. Whether you’re after a casual dinner or a place to treat yourself, it’s definitely worth a visit. This spot has easily become one of my go-to favourites on Brick Lane. The only negative,  the menu is far too big.

I had a great dinner time at this Thai restaurant for a date with my wife. The service was warm and attentive throughout the night- Imran in particular did a great job making sure we were looked after.

The food was absolutely delicious and beautifully presented. The mixed starters were very good and flavorful, with a great variety of sauces. The main dishes were just as impressive: the stir-fried noodles were rich and aromatic along with the beef dish. Both were nice and spicy which suited our preferences

Highly recommend for anyone looking for great Thai food and excellent service!

Amazing authentic Thai cuisine located in the heart of Brick Lane, the food was so flavoursome and the portion sizes were so generous, the ambience was really nice and the staff were so warm, friendly and attentive from the moment we stepped in right until we left. Brilliant service, would highly recommend!

From the moment we walked in, we were made to feel genuinely welcome at this lovely family-owned Thai restaurant. The service was outstanding — warm, attentive, and full of care, the kind that instantly makes you feel at home.

The food was absolutely exceptional. Every dish was clearly made with fresh ingredients, beautifully balanced flavours, and real passion for Thai cooking. From the starters to the mains, everything arrived perfectly cooked and full of depth, with generous portions and thoughtful presentation.

This is easily one of the best Thai restaurants I’ve visited, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to anyone — whether you’re local or happy to travel for great food. We’ll definitely be returning again and again.

name: Nom Nom Restaurant
address: 134 F-G, Kingsland Rd, London E2 8DY, UK

reviews.text:
After visiting the Home Museum, we walked across Nom Nom. Their décoration feels like local Vietnamese restaurant, so we decided to give it a try.

We ordered the Xeo Tofu Pancake, the Pork & Wood Ear Mushroom Steamed Rice Roll, and the Bun Cha Ha Hoi.
I highly recommend the Tofu Pancake — it’s incredibly fresh and flavorful, with a perfectly crunchy texture. The Bun Cha Ha Hoi is a cold noodle dish, but the grilled pork mixed with the noodles is surprisingly delicious. The rice rolls are soft, mild in flavor, and feel really light and healthy.

Overall, a great spot — definitely worth checking out!

Excellent  tasty food, baguette with caramelised  mushroom was fresh and bread was soft and crispy. Lamb curry and egg fried rice tasty seasoned well. Service was fairly quick, staff attentive and friendly.  Good portions sizes and excellent choice for vegans. Highly recommend.  Gets busy  lunch times and little noisy with kids but atmosphere  is relaxed. Reasonably priced our bill was £35 with drinks.

Amazing food and amazing service. Van is my absolute favourite person and part of the whole experience. The only reason I keep coming back apart from the obvious which how glorious the food is. Honestly I would consider myself a bit of a pho connoisseur seeing as I go out for pho all over London. This place is by far my favourite I could come back here forever and to see Van of course. Thank you for the drink on the house too, what wonderful service.

The food was soo delicious! The most authentic Vietnamese food I had in London. The service was really great, everyone was super nice. I can really recommend the place. We didn’t had a reservation for Saturday and still got a good table.

The food was so tasty and authentic! So many veggie/vegan options - I really recommend the crispy salt and pepper mushrooms and vegan wok fried noodles. Staff were super friendly and I can’t wait to go back again!

My interpretation is “making fine dining accessible,” which came through in a few ways:

Staff were friendly and relaxed. Still professional with the detail orientation and servicing of fine dining, but without the formalities. For example, they timed the food according to my pace, but didn’t make this obvious. In a break, they even shared a service dish.

Ambience reflects this. The open kitchen is small, with friendly, non-intimidating vibes. Details like both still water and sparkling water being on “tap” (free) in a pub-esque feel seems to be intentional.

Lastly, the food is not overly complex. Flavors come through without too much layering, but still hits texture, temperature, and finish. For example, the duck dish created variety by having breasts, liver pate, and confit. Bu flavors were honest, and simple.

Overall, great, accessible version of fine dining. Ordering many appetizers with drinks seems like a good fit for this one.

We had mistakenly booked for the incorrect number of people (too few) and the staff were courteous enough to quickly reseat us and ensure we had a great experience despite the mishap. The food was all incredible!! Highly recommend the crab salad, beef tartare, and the beef rib if it’s available on special. You can’t go wrong with anything here - the only mistake is if you don’t save room for the basque cheesecake and olive oil ice cream. Out of this world!

After trying multiple restaurants in London, I've come to the conclusion that British cuisine, in terms of flavours, is rather mundane and nothing out of the ordinary. Having said that, Brat definitely checked all the points for great food, though simple. Upon entering I liked how the hostess asked me where I wanted to sit and I was able to pick the table directly facing the kitchen.
I had the Anchovy bread and was able to see the chef kneading the dough then placing it into the oven with expertise, so satisfying! The bread itself was the usual, but the quality of the bread and the fish; just impeccable! For the main I had the John Dory and smoked potatoes, and gotta say it was sublime! The fish was peculiar in taste...in the best way possible; subtle hints of lemon and salt really elevated the dish. The potatoes were just as delicious with the right texture and crunch on the skin. For the dessert I got the burnt cheesecake with the fig; individually the components were nothing great, but when tasted all together, it was a burst of amazing sweetness and tartiness combined...a total win there! Though I would have liked the cake to have been softer (only because it is a Michelin star establishment) but otherwise, it satisfied my palate.
Service was friendly, and I liked how down to earth the demeanours of the servers were. Still, I would have appreciated if they'd asked if I wanted the potatoes to go while clearing out the table. In summary, a good place to grab a hearty meal once in a while!

Absolutely delicious! The food tasted so good and the quality was impeccable. The highlights were the squid, the venison, the mushrooms and eggs. Highly recommend! I really wanted to order the olive oil ice cream- price/quantity was pretty good seeing as it wasn’t too expensive considering the amount of food.
The only thing I’d suggest to improve is the size of the venue- it felt a little too crowded when it got busy.
9/10

We had a great evening at Brat Shoreditch. We sat at the bar which had a great view of the whole restaurant, which has a chilled atmosphere even though it was booked out. The service was great from start to finish, Shout out to our waiter, the man with the French accent who was attentive, friendly and super helpful when helping us decide what to order.
The food was simple but clever and beautiful, with delicate flavours and high quality ingredients. The stand out for us was the butternut squash with chestnuts and fresh cheese, the scallops, the monkfish and the olive oil ice cream. One of the best meals we’ve had in London. Will definitely return

This is the second time we come to The Sichuan and we love it. We feel the food is authentic and really tasty - Sichuan is spicy, so watch it if you don’t like it. a lot of options in the menu and we liked everything we ordered. Service is fast and friendly, Eva was really welcoming. Do recommend!

Lovely place with authentic Sichuan Chinese food. I ordered the spicy pig intestines and they we were great. Spicy, flavored and it came mixed with lotus root and potato. Super yummie. Portion was large. Staff was nice and attentive. Food was served quickly. Will come back.

A work friend and I came here following a meeting near by. The place was rammed to the gills with happy looking people eating what looked like amazing Chinese food. We spoke with Leslie who kindly found a table for us. Leslie gave out some excellent recommendations and was spot on with both choices. I had the House Special Fried Rice and my friend had the Beef dish. The food was prepared lightning fast and was both fresh and hot when it arrived. I had intentions of having dessert, however I was so full after the meal that there was no way. We plan on bringing some Team members here the next time. My friend’s Beef dish was huge and the Egg Fried Rice was light and fluffy. The House Special Fried Rice was one of the best I have ever had. The price was surprising given both the quality & quantity. Special thanks to Leslie for looking after us.

I recently tried this Sichuan restaurant, and it was absolutely amazing! The flavors were bold, authentic, and full of that signature numbing spice. The spicy pork trotters and Mao Xue Wang were the absolute highlights — rich, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. If you love real Sichuan heat, this place is a must-visit!
The food was authentic tasting. I enjoyed it a lot. Lesley was so lovely as well. Overall, what a lovely place to enjoy good food and a beer.

Great place, we visited this weekend. We ordered Moroccan tea, Ayran, Farrouj Meshwi, and Mixed Grills. The chicken was tender and juicy. The Mixed Grills are amazing; it's now my favorite dish. We were very pleased and will come back again.

The chicken and lamb grill were unbelievably juicy and full of flavor, and the baklava was the perfect sweet ending. The interior is beautiful with its colorful lanterns and cozy vibe, and the staff were very polite and welcoming. A must-visit spot for amazing food and great hospitality!

I'd call it a hidden gem. It's tucked away in Brick Lane, pretty easy to miss.
Atmosphere is good and food is right on spot: juicy, great mix of rice and vegetables and don't let the salad fool you. I wanted spicy and it was one of the spiciest I had in London.

Fantastic customer service from Anna, she’s an asset to the business!

The food was sensational and made to order - we had the mixed grill and the grilled sea bass.
delicious food and lovely ambience :)) the meat is so flavourful and juicy, and the owners are very nice too- definitely coming back again!!

We went for the lunch menu (there are three options); we opted for the lunch for £75 per person.
It was worth every penny.
From the very friendly welcome to the unhurried, excellent service and the atmosphere, this restaurant comes highly recommended!
The description of how each dish was prepared alone was enough to whet our appetite.
All the ingredients combined to create a perfect flavour.
It was great that the restaurant was open on a Monday, bucking the trend. We would definitely choose St. Bart's for dinner on our next visit to London.
We were happy and very excited as we set off for the rest of the day.
Thank you Rainer und Larissa

Just visited St. Barts, London’s new Michelin-star gem, and it truly stole my heart. The space is calm and relaxed, letting the food shine. Every dish—from the earthy Mushrooms & Roasted Yeast to the exquisite Game Bird Galantine, Crab with Horseradish & Buttermilk, and the stunning Chinese Water Deer—was precise, layered, and full of character. The £165 tasting menu is incredible value for a Michelin-star experience. Elegant, thoughtful, and unforgettable—St. Barts is easily my top dining pick in London this year.

Minimal lines, warm wood tones, and perfectly balanced lighting create an effortlessly elegant atmosphere. The tasting menu is precise and seasonal, with beautifully composed dishes that feel thoughtful rather than theatrical. A refined, quietly confident dining experience in London

My second visit to St Barts and it remains a calm, refreshing escape from the city noise. The cooking is thoughtful and ingredient focused, with lots of grains, game and fermentation, and you can really taste the care and technique behind each dish. Highlights included the beautifully cooked turbot, the well handled deer, and a deep, complex fermented barley dessert. A quietly impressive meal and well worth a return visit.

My wife and I had an amazing experience at St Barts. The food is amazing , the wine is extremely well paired and the staff very knowledgeable and friendly. We enjoyed the welcoming atmosphere, as well as the relaxed start in the lounge before heading to the table. A dinner night we will not forget!

name: Koya Japanese Restaurant Hackney
address: 10 Broadway Market Mews, London E8 4TS, UK

reviews.text:
The food here is bloody good BUT Jesus Christ All Mighty it's pricey! And small on the portion side sadly, so small that you need to grab a bag of Maltesers on the way home to feel fully satisfied, and maybe some chips, and a punnet of grapes... I seem to echo the sentimentality of most folks here, we're locals, we'd be coming more often but we'd like to eat every other day too rather than one bite here and then ration our pennies and ask for alms for the rest of the week.

All in all, the atmosphere is cool, food is great, and we love the staff that work there.

I ordered the KO Meaty Hot Udon, vegetable tempura, and a lemonade, everything was excellent.

The udon was deeply comforting and well balanced: a small amount of chilli oil added aroma and depth without making it greasy or overpowering, and the beef shin was incredibly tender and slow-cooked.

The vegetable tempura was also very well done, retaining the vegetables’ natural freshness and juiciness while having a light, crisp batter.

The restaurant itself is quite small, it probably seats around 30 people at most — so it can feel a bit crowded. The atmosphere is that of a cosy, casual Japanese eatery where people eat efficiently and move on. It’s not ideal if you’re looking to sit and chat for a long time.

That said, I didn’t mind at all, as I was dining alone. On a cold, rainy day, having a bowl of hot udon here was exactly what I needed 😆 warm, satisfying, and comforting.

Writing a good review for the kids menu alone, as it actually had healthy options which is so hard to find. I also find it hard to find more baby friendly restaurants in this side of London, so appreciate when they’re very welcoming to kids.

My son loved it and ate most of it! Kids food was around £8, we sat outside & they brought out a highchair for us :)

Nice small restaurant hidden away on the corner. I’ve had this on my “Want to go” list for a long time and finally visited today. I ordered the Mackerel Udon, Chicken Kaarage and Natto. Super delicious and fresh tasting. Definitely will return to try the other meals.

The food was amazing, I couldn’t believe I could have such proper Japanese udon in London. The atmosphere was super cozy and comfortable, and the staff were friendly and enthusiastic.
Love this place so much will defo come back again!

name: Baraka London
address: Unit 4, 1 Finsbury Ave, Broadgate, London EC2M 2PF, UK

reviews.text:
Baraka is an absolute gem. The food was rich, comforting, and beautifully presented, with flavours that felt both indulgent and balanced.

We ordered a mix of grills and mains — the kebabs were perfectly cooked, juicy and well-seasoned, with that smoky char you want from a proper grill. The chicken was tender, the lamb full of flavour, and the sides (especially the grilled vegetables and tomato) complemented everything really well.

One standout was the dish served in a deep, spiced tomato sauce topped with creamy yoghurt — hearty, warming, and incredibly satisfying. The bread and dips were fresh and moreish, and everything felt thoughtfully put together rather than rushed.

The cocktails were excellent too — refreshing, well-balanced, and a great match for the food. Add to that a stylish, relaxed atmosphere and attentive service, and it made for a really enjoyable evening.

Would definitely return — great spot for sharing plates, drinks, and a long catch-up.

Food was pretty good, people were very attentive and checks in frequently, nice bright place to have a great group meal. They also was able to accommodate big group - like 15 people at the back of the restaurant which was nice!

Bread was warm and fluffy and salad was fresh (mainly sour notes for dressing) and it's all downhill from there. Babaghanoush is tasteless beyond a bit of smokiness, the prawns were overcooked and tastes like what I made in university (and I am a bad cook). If you understand middle eastern and Asian cuisine - it's not for you it's more of a Great environment for corporate get together vibe. Lovely waitress.

The food was delicious and tender. We enjoyed it and it was tasty and the waiters were very welcoming. The atmosphere of the place was fantastic with lovely outdoor setting.
My experience with Turkish restaurants is that the portions are large; this wasn’t as large.
Also, no bread was brought while awaiting the mains.
Hummus was delicious. I got the salmon and loved the broccoli that came with it. Highly! Recommend. Great atmosphere and service. Excited to be back

Having dinner at The English Restaurant in London was such a great experience. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere felt warm and inviting, with that cozy, traditional pub-style charm mixed with a touch of elegance. It’s the kind of place that immediately makes you feel comfortable, whether you’re visiting for the first time or a regular.
The menu had plenty of classic British dishes, and everything we tried was delicious. I ordered the roast chicken, which was tender and full of flavor, while others at the table had the fish pie and a steak, both of which were excellent. The portions were generous without being over the top, and everything tasted freshly prepared. We also shared a sticky toffee pudding for dessert, which was the perfect sweet ending—rich, warm, and absolutely worth it.
The service was friendly and attentive, with the staff checking in just the right amount without being pushy. It felt like they genuinely cared about making sure we had a good experience.
Overall, dinner at The English Restaurant was the perfect mix of great food, a relaxed atmosphere, and wonderful service. I’d definitely recommend it for anyone wanting a true taste of British dining in London.

I got the lamb with mint sauce on there Sunday roast menu and it was delicious. The roast potatoes we perfect, crisp and fluffy. The leeks were some of the best I have had and the lamb was delicious. Highly recommend. I’m gluten intolerant so I couldn’t have the Yorkshire pudding but was accommodated well by the staff. I sat in a booth and the atmosphere was very nice a good level of noise and cozy decor. I will definitely be here again.

I had their bread and butter pudding with some coffee and banana bread - all of them were delightful. The pudding was creamy, not too heavy and had just the right amount of sweetness. The atmosphere is wonderful - had the nostalgia of an honest old English tavern. Lots of pictures and antiques. Would definitely visit again for dinner or supper.

This review is for breakfast. And I love coming here for it each time I’m in London.

Food: Breakfast! Weekend breakfasts are tops as they do the Full English then, but weekday breakfasts tick the box too. I had the Eggs Benedict – eggs cooked to a runny perfection with the most delicious hollandaise on a lightly toasted English muffin. And a supporting flat white to wash it down with.

Service: Friendly and attentive without hovering.

Space: A great spot to work out of (quiet work, don’t do your calls here folks, please) and enjoy a beverage and a meal. I can’t say they’ll be OK with folks hogging a table at peak times but I’ve only ever been there pre-lunch.

Cost: So very reasonable for central London, about £25 for breakfast and a coffee.

Takes cards and cash. Give it a go!

I loved the inside of this pub. Super cute and cozy, with friendly service and pretty good food. We came for breakfast and had the eggs with smoked salmon and the French toast. They also served a pretty decent flat white. Everything was reasonably priced as well. We came around 9:30 AM on a Saturday morning and it was not too crowded yet. Would definitely come back.

name: Sotto Cucina & Bar
address: Black Lion House, 45 Whitechapel Rd, London E1 1DU, UK

reviews.text: Not Sicilian. This is not focaccia. This is not busiate pasta. This is not broccoli almond Sicilian busiate. This is mediocre “Italian-ish” at best. 2 stars because it was just barely edible. Benefit of the doubt: Line cooks are just doing what they’re told but the leadership of this restaurant needs to take a long hard look at themselves. Plenty of competition nearby.

We had our friend's baby shower for 20 here, and it was a lovely experience.

The private room space was nice with very cute 'green' wall, decor was tasteful and space did not feel cramped. Staff were nice and friendly.

Food was tasteful and good portions. Came out warm and decorated nicely. The service for dessert was a bit slow, and the menu did not include all options (juice and coffee not on main menu) but staff were accommodating.

This place is part of Hyatt hotel but we did not stay to have lunch here. Note there is a separate venue hire of £200.
Part of a Hyatt Hotel. Food and Drinks were ok but nothing special or extraordinary. You can eat there but there are definitely better italien restaurants in the area and in town.

Excellent service and delicious food! A hidden gem located on the lower ground floor of Hyatt Hotel. We went on a Friday night and it was not too busy, nice atmosphere. We went during The Fork Festival so we had 50% off food which was amazing value. Spent £83 between 3 of us including a bottle of wine and orange juice.

We are currently staying at the Hyatt Place. The food in both Sotto Cucina Bar and Pocket Square is remarkable. Fresh ingredients, attention to detail and the flavours are beautiful.

All the staff are attentive and helpful. Our breakfast beauty Daniel is genuinely one of the loveliest people we have ever met. Such a flair for hospitality and clearly loves what he does. We really felt it should be recognised. Thank you Daniel for making our morning memorable and for the amazing service and smiles!

Highly recommend a stay here and you will not be disappointed with the choice of food and the excellent customer service.

Amazing experience! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
They offer excellent gluten-free options, clearly indicated and with real awareness of cross-contamination, which made me feel completely safe. The pasta was delicious, perfectly cooked, and with an incredible texture — just as good as the traditional one.

The staff was very attentive and friendly, happy to answer questions and taking great care of every detail. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, perfect for a relaxed meal without worries.

Without a doubt, one of the best Italian restaurants for gluten-free dining. We will definitely come back! 🍝

It was my first time trying this Italian restaurant in London, and I was truly impressed. The pasta is handmade fresh every day, and the taste was absolutely amazing  incredibly delicious and full of authentic flavor.
I also had the honour of meeting Sandra, who took wonderful care of me and my father. Her service was warm, attentive, and made our experience even more special.
I will definitely be coming back with my friends and my whole family. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for fantastic Italian food and outstanding hospitality.

My gluten-free partner was beyond satisfied. We will be back to try everything else on the menu.

You’ve never seen a human so happy that they could order gluten free lasagne with *bread*. The food was £££ but for coeliac-friendly pasta - it was 100% worth it.

The restaurant is nice, although looks a little unfinished in places.

The service was friendly and efficient. Total lack of atmosphere because it was empty and freezing cold.

If you’ve fallen for the hype on TikTok, this is not going to tick all of your boxes - it isn’t a stunning restaurant with instagrammable interiors and loads of choice. But it does have an excellent choice of gluten-free, well presented pasta with bread that is warm, pillowy and tasty. It is probably the best gluten-free bread we’ve ever had in a restaurant (but that bar is not a high one!).

You can make a Saturday out of it and go to Spitalfields after for GF Cakes from the Polka Dot Bakery 🌾 🍰

If you want somewhere nice, safe and delicious without worrying about cross-contamination - book here and book soon.

So so so disappointing. I was looking forward to coming as i saw gluten free TikTokers post about the ‘amazing, hand made fresh pasta’. In the one photo is the pasta I was told i’d get, in another photo is the shop-bought pasta i got, which is identical to the ready done one i get from sainsburys all the time. And we waited over and hour for it. Real shame. Out bill was £80’each for this.

Best gluten free Italian I’ve ever had! The service is superb and the food is absolutely delectable. We had the crescentine (I couldn’t believe it was GF) and insalata to start with, Tagliatelle al Ragu Bolognese and their special Balanzoni filled with mortadella and ricotta was amazing. We finished with the tiramisu and cheesecake, and it was all gluten free, no hassle, no worries, absolutely delicious.

name: Galata Restaurant & Bistro
address: City Road Lock, Regent's Canal Towpath, London N1 8PZ, UK

reviews.text:
A great place to eat. Now on my staycation list.

I have not tasted calamari like this before. No over crisped coating, not oily and very flavoursome. I enquired about the coating used and was advised it was cornflour, so hopefully that info is correct.

I usually go for the octopus, which comes with chips and salad.

They do get busy, but the setting along the canal makes it worth it, especially when the weather is good.

We popped into this local pizzeria for a quick lunch on a rainy Saturday and it was perfectly decent — nothing mind-blowing, but solid enough that we'd probably return if we're in the area.
The place has a nice casual vibe: wooden tables, some Italian music in the background, and friendly (if a bit rushed) staff. We ordered a classic Margherita and a Pepperoni to share, plus a couple of soft drinks.
The pizzas came out fairly quickly — thin-ish crust, which we like, with a good char on the edges from the oven. The tomato sauce was tasty and herby, mozzarella melted nicely without being greasy, and the pepperoni had decent spice. Nothing super fresh or artisanal like some of the fancy Neapolitan spots, but miles better than chain takeaway. One small gripe: the base got a bit soggy in the middle from the toppings, and it could've used a touch more seasoning overall.

Mackerel was served with delicious fries and a generous salad, also, deal comes with a soft drink. Their Chai Iced Latte was really nice too! You can enjoy beautiful views of the canal while enjoying a nice lunch. Good place!
Food was OK. The coffee was real good. Worth a visit for idyllic seating and watching the world go by

Bar / coffee shop by the canal with seating area outside. Perfect views and the food was delicious (and cheap being in mind we are in London!). We order calamari and were very tasty, soft and spicy. It comes with ketchup and tartare sauce. Also they have available different sauces, like mayonnaise and so… Today the terraza was fine but if the weather is good, they used to be very busy

name: Ara Restaurant
address: 1 New Drum St, London E1 7AY, UK

reviews.text:
We ended up eating lunch here almost by chance as it was close to our hotel, and honestly didn’t expect much — but it turned out to be a really good surprise.

For around £30–40 per person, the food was much better than expected and felt like great value. The courgette dip was a standout straight away. It was super smooth, really flavourful, and not at all bland like you might expect from a vegetable-based dish. We ordered bread with it and kept going back for more — easily one of the best things we had.

The beef croquettes were also excellent. Crispy on the outside, soft and rich on the inside, and full of proper beef flavour. They didn’t feel greasy or heavy, and the sauce that came with them worked really well without taking over.

Overall, everything felt well thought out without being fussy or overcomplicated. The food was just done properly. The atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable, and the service was friendly and easygoing, which made it a really nice place to spend the day.

What started as a random choice because of location turned into one of the better meals we had during the trip. Would definitely come back and happily recommend it — especially for the courgette dip and beef croquettes

My friend and I came here for brunch today and absolutely loved it. We arrived early and were seated straight away, given menus, and offered bottled water. The decor is beautiful and the atmosphere instantly felt relaxed and welcoming.

We shared the shakshuka, beef croquettes, burrata, and a mushroom dish, and everything was outstanding - full of flavour, beautifully presented, and clearly made with care. There was a small mix-up with the mushrooms and we were brought the mushroom dumplings instead of the roasted mushrooms listed on the menu, but it turned out to be a very happy accident as the dumplings were incredible and exactly what we’d hoped to order after seeing them online.
The service really stood out. Our waiter was genuinely friendly, attentive, and made us feel so comfortable. When the bill arrived, we noticed the mushroom dish hadn’t been added. The waiter explained it was his mistake and kindly insisted on not charging us, which was such a thoughtful and generous touch.
We stayed on for more hot drinks and were happily allowed to sit and chat while the rain passed, which just added to the calm, cosy vibe of the restaurant. It was such a relaxing and enjoyable experience overall.

I can’t recommend this place highly enough and will definitely be back soon with a bigger group to try more of the menu!

A very enjoyable evening at the Ara restaurant in Aldgate. All the dishes were extremely tasty and beautifully prepared... the waiter gave us some great tips on what to order.
We left the Ara feeling full and very satisfied. We highly recommend it!
Thank you.

The best experience I had in London in the last year.
Great place, great and quick service, great food presentation, nice innovative ideas, great taste really good prices. I hope they carry on like this for a long time, so I can come back often. Excellent surprise.

Frb26- wonderful vibes, and decor.
Small sharing plate menu. Six people had cornx2, trout, dumplings, cabbage, leeks,  croquettes, potatoes, potato bread, and beetroot.
£210 with a 20% off voucher.
Mixed bag - the use of smoke first is interesting then just overpowering (hake/roackbass was unpleasant imho). Best beetroot, light kimchi, and good trout.
Extremely helpful staff happy to accommodate dietary concerns and the wine was good.
Hackney vibes. Brilliant vegan pizza, got the truffle mushroom and nduja. The chilli oil is nicely v spicy, and garlic oil brilliant with cashew parmesan 😍 They use "I am nut ok" vegan cheese.

Best bar in Hackney, with incredible views over London's skyline. Amazing cocktails and the pizza is 10/10 for me. Make sure you get the truffle mayo!!

Really great vibe up there soundtracked by some of the finest DJ talent around too. Make sure you get up there for sunset!

Nice bar but a girl in our group (who arrived alone) was denied entry for allegedly having a “faulty” drivers license, so we all left. Don’t risk it!

We booked Netil360 for a group of 12. One girl in our party (who is, as we are, 28 years old) arrived slightly later so queued up alone and showed her drivers license to security as usual, but he proceeded to scratch the hologram off the card and assert that this meant it was not a real license. We tried to speak to the manager to explain that this was an old format license, but he already decided that this girl would not be allowed in because she had been rude to security (she had incredulously declared “you’re taking the piss” when he scratched the card). A photo of a passport was also denied. Without wanting to abandon our friend, our entire party left (we’d had 1 round of drinks). Not to worry though: Mare Street Market was right next door and had much friendlier and understanding staff! No problem with other bars in the area either.

Overall a disappointing and completely unexpected experience. Something needs to be done about this obstinate door policy…

It’s a Really good atmosphere here the rooftop is good in the summer, the food is really good, but I’m scoring it average as the service was awful. I Got given the same order number as someone else and food got mixed up which is fine if you amend it and are sorry. But the pizza staff tried to say it’s my fault and that I ordered 1 totally different pizza when I ordered two. Then I proved I did via my bank statement. Then they told me to wait and got my order wrong a second time. Which i was fine about as I was drinking and having a good time, then when my pizza’s finally came I got no apology, no cutlery or sauces and a angry fed up look. Might just be a one off but they need competent staff working on orders.
A well-maintained restaurant where the experience feels measured and consistent. The visit flows smoothly, and nothing interrupts the calm and balanced rhythm of the stay.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I had a great experience at Bella Villa, a lovely Italian restaurant. I ordered the grilled fish and it was absolutely delicious—fresh, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor. The ambiance was warm and welcoming, and the staff were friendly and attentive. Definitely a place I’d love to visit again. Highly recommended!

Staff were literally the sweetest ever and honestly had the best Italian food in London, so authentic and it’s so difficult to find good halal Italian in London. Highly recommend! Portions were generous and staff were so welcoming and nice to us. Interior was clean, nice and cosy. Can’t recommend the place enough tbh. Do check them out

I brought my partner and 3 kids and ordered seafood linguine, pizza, chicken, salmon and spaghetti bolognaise. Food was very fresh and delicious service kind and courteous! Will absolutely return asap

I dined at this authentic Italian restaurant during my trip to London and loved Bella Villa! My favorite was the Linguina Gamberi pasta, bruschetta and the Bella Villa special. Also, don’t miss out — make sure you get the delicious tiramisu!
Went to Bella Villa Italian Restaurant with friends and loved it! The spaghetti Bolognese was amazing and full of flavor. Really happy they serve halal food too. Great place to eat and relax

name: Taş Fırın Turkish Restaurant - Shoreditch
address: 160 Bethnal Grn Rd, London E2 6DG, UK

reviews.text:
If you’re looking for incredible Turkish food, you have to visit Taş Fırın 🤍

The mezes were absolutely delicious — so good that I completely forgot to take a picture before we started eating! That’s how amazing they were 😅 I’ll post the photo of the plate… but only after we finished it because we couldn’t wait to dig in!

Every dish we tried was fresh, full of flavour, and cooked to perfection.

What truly makes this place special is the hospitality. The warmth and kindness make you feel so welcome from the moment you walk in.

Highly recommend — such a beautiful dining experience! ✨

This was recommended to us and we went today. I appreciate the staff a lot! we had a couple of flower bouquets with us and they lent us a little bucket for them to stand properly! One female staff even came to ask us about the flowers and complimented how nice smelling they are. They seem to have a lot of regulars come in and they look like great friends. Really great food but interactions like that make a restaurant so much better!!

I had a wonderful experience at Tas Fırın Restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious — fresh, flavourful, and perfectly prepared.

A special shout-out to waitress Dilek, who truly made the visit memorable. She is incredibly kind, attentive, and genuinely lovely. Her friendly service added so much to the experience.

I highly recommend Tas Fırın to anyone looking for great food and amazing hospitality. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Lovely people and excellent food. They make you feel truly welcome and special, and there is a great atmosphere inside. Families, friends, coworkers. Large parties or intimate dates. No one zoned out on their phone but truly connecting and being present. A real place, lucky it was next to our AirbNb

I’ve been coming to eat at this restaurant for almost 4 years now. The food is always perfect and delicious, big menu with enough options and home made food. But the best thing here is the service and their staff, they always make me feel like at home. A must if you’re in the shoreditch area

Really enjoyed this, was like a mini holiday.

I had the Beef Bentobab which was surprising in that the flavours were quite delicate. The Chicken Dumplings were very tasty - just a little tricky with the stainless steel chopsticks, but I managed!

Loved the atmosphere so will definitely go back to try their other recipes.

Staff very friendly.

Only warning- tables are very close together

This is my go to restaurant for Korean cuisine. Try to book a table beforehand, but even if you don’t, the restaurant is fast moving and they do take walk-ins. They also have BBQ (which I have tried) and Karaoke (which I have not). Overall, you can’t go wrong here. My favourite dishes are Glazed Chicken BBQ Bibimbap , Dolsot Bibimbap, Korean fried chicken, kimchi fried rice and bao bun. It’s not a place where you can spend a lot of time, but the food is one of the best and service is excellent.

Good food, $$.we had kimchi set, steamed rice,kimchi pancake,  2 KFC small & medium,3 Galib Tang, Gugeolopan, A good amount for 6 people. Good quality on the meats. Service was very efficient.  A good place in that area for K-pop food. As always, post wherever your palate takes you.

Had a very pleasant time dining here food was great and staff were very polite and friendly. The atmosphere is welcoming and well designed. A huge shout out to “RIA”, who was so sweet and helpful. She was incredibly kind, attentive, and made our meal even more enjoyable. We’ll definitely be back!

I recently dined in at Bentobab, and it was honestly a great experience from start to finish. The place has a clean, cozy atmosphere simple but nicely done, and it feels comfortable whether you’re there alone or with friends. The staff were genuinely friendly and attentive without being pushy, which made the whole visit feel relaxed.

The food was the real highlight. Everything came out fresh, nicely presented, and full of flavor. You can tell they use good ingredients and actually care about what they’re serving. The dishes had that perfect balance tasty but not heavy, well-seasoned but not overdone. My order arrived quickly, and even the side dishes felt thoughtfully prepared, not like an afterthought.

What I really liked is that the portions were fair, and you could enjoy the meal without feeling rushed. The place was clean, including the tables and wash area, which says a lot about how well they manage the restaurant.

Overall, Bentobab is a spot I’d definitely visit again. Whether you’re coming for a quick bite or a proper meal, it’s worth it. Good food, great service, and a chill environment that’s hard to find all in one place. Highly recommend trying it out if you haven’t yet.

Everything was amazing. People help us decide what best suits for us. They where very helpful. Food was amazing, service as well! Highly recommend. Really!! They treat you like a family which is incredible.  Please come in and help this guys ❤️❤️

On arrival a bit quiet but I visited on a Saturday however this picked up during my time at the restaurant.
Great food & wine choice. Food was extremely tasty. Service was excellent.

Lovely Turkish restaurant in the city. It’s very spacious so good for a team lunch/dinner also. In the summer they have a nice outdoor space also. The food is always very good quality and speedy so can’t fault the service

Great location, and great atmosphere.
The food was tasty, and it was made ready pretty quickly which we appreciated.
The waiter/waitress and the staff were unamused, bored and had very little patience and attention for us. This place would not be my first option if I'm in the area because if the mediocre service.

I booked a table of 14 to celebrate a special occasion and they dealt with my enquiry so smoothly and seamlessly. The night went extremely well and our waitress handled everything with ease. The food was delicious; I went for the tiger prawn dish. I would greatly recommend booking with HAZ for your special occasions, the food and service are incredible and so is the atmosphere.

name: Barcelona Tapas Bar & Restaurant
address: Barcelona Tapas Bar & Restaurant 1 Middlesex Street, E1 7AA (OFF St Botolph Street, London EC3A 7DT, London E1 7AA, UK

reviews.text: This was recommended to me through my native Spanish friend so knew it would be good. Amazing staff very attentive I really left smiling because they’re were just so friendly they allowed me to try out my broken Spanish with ease ha. The foood wow 😮 so good great price near the city and we could hardly walk from the amount of food we had please try the seafood paella and pork crackling massive highlights for us

We visited this restaurant for a quick dinner, but we were thoroughly disappointed. The food was poorly prepared, oily, and had an unusual mix of spices that didn’t align with the cultural expectations we had. To add to our dismay, the restaurant was dirty, with disgusting toilets. The overall atmosphere was noisy and unwelcoming. Despite the staff’s kindness and friendliness, we left everything on the table and left the restaurant.

Food 0/5
Cleanliness 1/5
Staff 4/5

Overpriced and not worth the heartburn you’ll get.

Not bad, I am hoping to return with company so I can try their paella. It's pricey but it's worth the taste. The portions are small, which I didn't realize until after the one item I wanted to have came. Staff seemed nice.
I tried the octopus (Pulpo al Gallega), which I had expected to come on a bed of sliced potatoes, instead they did mash. It was really tasty.

I started the dinner with Botata with garlic sauce it was really nice, then the calamari crunchy and Yummi, after that i eat my special main dish Bayella 😍❤️ i adore it, if it was without chicken would be better ❤️

We ended up at Barcelona Tapas Bar by accident after a change of plans - and we’re glad we did. The food was great, portions generous, and everything felt authentic. The sangria was especially good, and the staff were warm and welcoming throughout. The space has a relaxed, cosy feel that made for a really nice evening. Would definitely come back.

We truly enjoyed our recent dining experience at your establishment. The ambiance was warm and inviting, creating a lovely atmosphere for our meal. Our server was attentive, the happy hour was great. The flavors of the dishes were authentic and beautifully presented.

The combination of Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine is incredibly delicious and new style of taste.
The salad was fresh, main course salmon and the white rice were good.
The portion was big and enough for one person.
The atmosphere and decoration provided tranquility with the ambient lightening.

I visited Haz Bishopsgate this week with a group of eight colleagues for an early evening booking. The restaurant was reasonably busy, and we were seated upstairs quickly which was a good start. There was a brief wait before we managed to get someones attention for drinks, as our first request was missed, but once the waiter came over things picked up. Fresh bread, olives and drinks followed shortly after. We ordered a mixed starter platter and had asked for the vegetarian items to be served separately for one colleague. This was acknowledged, although everything eventually arrived across two platters rather than fully separated. Not a major issue, but worth noting. For my main, I had the Chicken Shish Kofte which was soft and succulent. The mains arrived promptly, and by this point the staff were much more attentive. It is a busy restaurant and, unlike some places where waiters check in regularly, there was naturally less of that here given the pace and volume of diners. Overall, a good experience with tasty food and the atmosphere you would expect from a popular City restaurant during the evening rush.

Really nice food. The starters and the mains were great. I had the sikander chicken dish. It was really nice. The only thing is that it's very loud when full (as you'd expect) so not the best place for having a full fledged conversation but otherwise really nice restaurant.

The meat here is halal.

Popped in for a drink and ordered a snack.  Nice bar area, didnt go into the restarant, cocktail was made well, snack was mediocre the one with goats cheese and spinach.  I would try the restaurant though as it wouldn't put me off trying it as the spicy sauce was delicious

name: Koya Japanese Restaurant City of London

reviews.text: The starters we ordered were a major let down: The cucumber & seaweed salad was bland and watery with no real taste, the fried prawns heads again had no seasoning and tasted of nothing other than oil (had to season myself with the chilli powder provided on each table) and finally the ‘special’ grilled octopus was again bland and appeared to just be boiled not grilled. However the udon dishes themselves were amazingly delicious. I had ordered the spiced cumin lamb udon - the amount of flavour that packed was top quality. Will be back to just try the other udon dishes for sure. Service was quality and attentive and the vibe of the restaurant was great!!

What a big disappointment on my visit. I cannot believe the price and the quality presented are so bad.

Start of with the starter. The portion is so small and its barely a bite to share between people. And they charge 9.9 for some veg  which is still freezing cold = straight out from the fridge. It doesnt even cost much if you double the portion.
Pork belly is the only normal dishes, however its still not tender enough. A good pork belly should not even need to use your teeth to tear apart, it should be melting in your mouth.
The grill octopus - I cannot believe how rip off this dish is charging people £17.10 for 5 pieces of chewing gum considering how thin the slices are. The veg next to it is seasoned with some miso, mustard, yuzu lemon and it is so salty, it is almost sea water salty and you cant even finish it with those jam thick sauce. Given £17 you should at least give a leg of octopus instead of few pieces of chewing gum to serve to your customer especially it doesn’t taste good at all.
The udon is also big disappointment charging 16.90 for a small udon, rockets coriander, and a small scoop of lamb mince. In terms of portion, I cannot believe how small it is. We paid £17 and you give me a scoop of lamb mince that probably cost you less than 10p??? Rockets and coriander - what kind of japanese culture serve these two with udon? You just put some cheap veg to make the colour looks good on the udon? The udon itself is not even marugame quality and they sell it for just less than £6.
I have rarely given any restaurants a one star review in my entire google review journey but this is definitely one of the most overrated, overhyped, overpriced, undeserving restaurants that I have ever visited. It is a disgrace to the Japanese culture if you serve this kind of food to any customer. I would not ever visit again and I strongly suggest the management need to review their price, quality, quantity. What a big disappointment.
Overall we spent more than £36 per person for these.

Nourishing, warming udon. Comfort in a bowl. Highly recommend.

Went to Koya (City of London Outlet) for lunch on Sat 17/12/2025. No reservation. Turned up and had to wait around in the front lobby area for maybe 15-20 minutes. Venue capacity doesn’t meet demands, staff a bit clueless on how to handle the constant influx of people, lots just standing around.

First came the tonkotsu pork. Crunchy but not sharp, juicy but not soggy, firm but not rubbery. Portion size was pretty good too and the salt on the side is a nice touch. Only problem is it cost £20. Honestly, I don’t think it was worth £20. Even for London that’s too much.

Next came the beef udon. I only got beef because the pork udon was sold out, turned out a blessing in disguise. Beef was tender and fell apart, with a strong depth of flavour. The noodles were springy and al dente, broth rich and warm. Portion size of both beef and noodle was also good. The £16.50 price tag is very reasonable.

I got tempura prawns on the side. I was initially sceptical of the huge batter idea, but I came around; adding batter to broth and eating it is a carby delight, a guilty pleasure. No such thing as excessive. For £5? Not great not terrible price, worth it.

Service was decent, although not noteworthy. Atmosphere was quite cramped.

Price was ~£40. This is quite a lot higher than it should have been in retrospect but most of that is driven by the tonkatsu pork, which isn’t good value for money. If you want a higher quality, fancier udon, Koya is a safe bet. Alternatively, if you want a far cheaper but almost as delicious udon, try Marugame near Liverpool Street Station.

With the cold weather setting in, my wife and I were looking for some comfort eats in London and came across Koya serving authentic and creative takes on udon noodle soups from Japan.

We started our meal with slow braised rice wine pork belly and agedashi tofu from their specials menu. We followed the starters with thin-cut pork belly served in udon noodle soup. The flavors from the pork and udon were absolutely delicious!

If you’re looking for good udon and braised pork belly in the city with Japanese cuisine flavors, I highly recommend Koya.

What a place this is! From the moment you walk through the doors, you’re transported to an authentic Japanese restaurant. We were greeted by a friendly member of staff and we sat at one of the bar tables. From here you have a full panoramic view of the open kitchen, watching everyone busily prepare food. Everything was cooked with precision and care whilst presentation was second to none. The food was delicious, and well seasoned with a range of different sauces and herbs for accompaniment. Nothing was over powering on the pallet and everything was cooked to perfection. I recommend if you get the chance to also sample their Sake tasting board. 3 small shots of different sake to try. Personally I’m not a drinker, but I found these samples to be amazing and I’m glad I had that experience. The duck in their duck kamo was tender and melted in the mouth. Would definitely look to come back again next time in London.

name: Restaurant Elis
address: 1st floor, Town Hall Hotel, 8 Patriot Square, London E2 9NF, UK

reviews.text:
It was good overall. But I was expecting more because it is the same chef as da terra. The brazilian bites (pastel, bolinho de peixe, and pao de queijo slider) were the lows for me. I think it could be way more interesting with a twist or something. I felt like I was paying 4 pounds in 1 item while in brazil you get 10 paying less than that with the same quality. Same goes to the pizza pastel.😅
I really enjoyed the pork chop and cassava chips, so good. It was a good experience but I was expecting more for the price we paid.

Had exceptional food looked after by Richard who guided us amazingly through the menu. Food was fantastic especially the pao de quejo slider, the croquettes and the trout.

Was a bit quiet but it is mid January. Music was great but was fairly quiet which is understandable this time of year. Would recommend to anyone who wants to try Brazilian cuisine !

This place was a little different. Not a lot of selections on the menu and the larger dishes are specials. The lamb skewer special was amazing. The cheese bread slider was pretty good as well. The bread baskets was good and my colleagues enjoyed their drinks. I almost gave it a 4 cause some of the dishes weren't as good, but the lamb was so good I had to round up to a five for this one.

Just happened to stumble upon this on Google maps on a Saturday evening, not having had (up to this point) good Brazilian food in London.

The restaurant is in a hotel, which made me a bit sceptical at first. But by the end of the dinner we weren't disappointed.

The place is small. Service was very friendly and welcoming. There were surprisingly few people there for a Saturday, which was even more surprising considering how good it was.

We ordered two of each of the Bolinhos de Bacalhau, Pastel de Pizza, Pão de Queijo sliders, and lamb skewers. We also ordered their special rice and seafood dish as a main.

The Bolinhos were nice and crisp, and the sliders were a fun take on Pão de Queijo (Brazilian cheese bread). The lamb was so tender and flavorful. The star of the show was the rice and seafood. The seafood and the rice were cooked to perfection. The amount of flavor in that rice was amazing.

All the while service was very attentive. The food came fast, but as a good pace -- they waited until we were done with one dish before getting the other.

I would definitely go there again, especially since it seems that they have different specials.

Cozy and gorgeous restaurant with great food and service. We were 3 people and had several starters and 2 mains. The taco was so good which was recommended by the server and the prawn pasta and sirloin steak with truffle were amazing. It’s a great place for a special day and also for a nice night out. I want to highlight that the server Chloe was giving us an impeccable service:) She was warm and polite, also recommendation for our order was so clear and appropriate. She made our experience more comfortable and memorable. I would definitely visit again.

Visiting London on a work trip. I wanted to try some Indian Food from here since I've heard it's some of the best. The service was great. My server was very attentive and asked me about my tastes preferences. The menu can be a bit overwhelming because there are just so many options.

The food was beyond amazing! The spice level was perfect at a medium.  I could have went more, but I think it would take away the enjoyment of the meal.  The main course was a lot. I think it be happy to have split the meal with one person. I'd go here again when I visit in the future.  Highly recommend!
Great delicious food and service. Worth the price and they honoured the discount. Would definitely recommend
The place was packed but we still received service as if we were the only people there.  Perfect!  Food was incredible as always.  Every time we are in London we head here.

Just wanted to try a chicken tikka masala when visiting London. But they had a meal set with different dishes to taste. Was great to try more dishes. Everything was delicious! Well prepared!
Would recommend a visit.

Portion size is large, so you can expect to be pretty full afterwards, if you even finish the portion. So nothing for a „small meal“ or quick light portion. Portions are massive 👍.

My wife had been before, so she already knew what to expect, but for me it was something completely new. We were slightly pressed for time as we had a train to catch back up north, so I was a little worried about queues and delays. Sure enough, when we arrived there was already a queue forming outside, and the weather looked like it was about to turn. Thankfully, the team at Dishoom were quick to act – we were seated outside almost immediately, and service began straight away. That efficiency made a big difference, as it meant we could relax and enjoy the meal without clock-watching.

The setting itself was welcoming, even outdoors. Despite the looming rain, the atmosphere carried the lively, bustling energy that jaipur is known for. There’s a sense that you’re part of something bigger than just a restaurant – more like a communal dining experience where everyone is there for the same reason: good food and a warm vibe. By the time we were leaving, the rain had just started to fall, which made the timing feel almost perfect.

As for the food, it really was excellent. Everything we ordered arrived quickly and was cooked to perfection. jaipur has a reputation for bold, flavourful Indian dishes that balance authenticity with modern touches, and that was exactly what we experienced. From the seasoning to the presentation, nothing felt rushed despite our limited time. It’s rare to feel both unhurried and well-looked after in such a busy spot, but the staff managed it brilliantly.

Overall, taste of jaipur was a fantastic first-time experience for me. Efficient service, delicious food, and great timing meant we left full, happy, and on schedule for our train.

name: Italina385
address: 385 Cambridge Heath Rd, Bethnal Green, London E2 9RA, UK

reviews.text:
I’ve been coming to Italina for years and have never been disappointed.

The owners are incredibly friendly, and the service is always fast and attentive.

Over the years, I’ve tried pretty much every pizza on the menu and every single one has been amazing, the dough is unbelievably good… Great wine selection too.

The tiramisu is also a favourite, super light, creamy, and full of flavour.

Hands down the best pizzeria in East London!

It's a low key neighnbourhood Italian in Bethnal Green that probably mostly supplies locals with pizzas, but is a surprisingly terrific restaurant.  Not living in the area, we were last here maybe eight years ago, but I still remember the pasta alla vongole I had on that occasion.  We've been to a lot of more expensive, and more famous Italians in London, but this place really reminds me of eating at trattorias on vacation in Italy.  Simple menu, terrific ingredients cooked in a way you can taste the individual components, and everything homemade.  They do serve dried pasta, which I actually prefer because its texture is more chewy.

My companion had the bruschetta to start followed by the burrata served on a bed of  grilled vegatables.  Both of his starters came with a fantastic focaccia which had big airy bubbles toasted to a crisp.  There was a tiny drizzle of pesto on the burrata that looked bright green and  tasted homemade.  I didn't taste the bruschetta, but my companion praised the sparing use of red onion in the tomato mix, making it perfectly balanced.

I had the scialatelli alla vongole, of course, with a side of the grilled vegetable salad with goat cheese.  I asked them to just bring both dishes as ready because I didn't want to eat them in sequence.  That's exactly how I got them, with the grilled veg first, and the pasta maybe 5 minutes later to eat along side.  My partner got his two starters in non overlapping sequence, exactly as requested as well.

The vongole was great.  There were maybe 8 clams in shells decorating the dish but plenty more shelled clams stirred through the pasta.  The clams were perfectly cooked and still tender and juicy.  I liked the restrained use of fresh cherry tomato sauteed in olive oil, which didn't dominate.  I could taste the good quality olive oil. The thick scialatelli was delightfully chewy.  It wasn't quite as spectacular as the version I ate on my last visit eight years ago, which included an unorthodox quantity of garlic.  Maybe next time I will ask if the current chef is willing to put in a little garlic for me.  The grilled vegetable salad with a thin slice of toasted goat cheese was excellent.  On top of the mixed green salad there were slices of grilled courgette, grilled eggplant and very sweet strips of peeled red pepper.  I was happy to note that the roasted pepper was homemade, having no hint of the acidic preservatives that peeled roast peppers from a jar has.

The cheapest bottles of wine are £29 and £30, and dinner including a bottle of red came to £78.  Music and noise levels are low.  There was an 80s pop soundtrack playing during our visit. We will definitely be back and won't wait eight years before our next visit.
Really amazing Italian place! Some of the best Italian I have had in London. Authentic and really tasty. I had the clams and my partner had an amazing beef ragu

Great and tasty traditional Italian restaurant! Service was great and fast, kind staff, and very flavorful pizzas. Tiramisu as dessert is very recommended, creamy and traditional. Overall very recommended, plus the location seem very traditional, it felt as being in a small restaurant in Italy!

It's hard to find good pizza nowadays around London and Italina it's a place for a proper Italian pizza. The food was amazing and I truly mean it. I have enjoyed every single bite of food. Everything was just spot on. I really do recommend this tiny Italian restaurant.
