I love the honemade pasta so much, especially the tomato sauce with Italian sausage, it's outstanding.  You mustn't miss this.  The sfogliattella is a must try item, you will not regret the smoothly orange  flavoured ricotta cheese filling.  The. pastry is crunchy!  Love this cafe so much

The service is wonderful, very friendly.

name: Smoking Goat Shoreditch
address: 64 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ, UK

reviews.text:
I’d been wanting to try The Smoaking Goat for a long time, and we finally took the opportunity when some friends came to visit. It was absolutely worth the wait!

First, I have to mention the great service. Our waitress was incredibly attentive and friendly. We couldn’t decide between 2 white wines, and she kindly brought us a glass of each to taste before choosing, such a thoughtful gesture! We ended up going with the 2023 Portuguese white, Intervalo Branco.

We decided to share several dishes between the five of us, and ordered:
Fried Chicken, Tom Yum and Pork, Massaman Bavette, Pad Phet Trout and Courgette, Squid and Salted Duck Egg with Courgette, Cabbage and Mushroom Soy Sauce, Daikon Som Tam, three House Rotis, Jasmine Rice, and BBQ Turmeric Gurnard.

The only dish I wouldn’t particularly recommend was the Cabbage and Mushroom Soy Sauce.
Everything else was fantastic!

My top recommendations would be the BBQ Turmeric Gurnard, the Squid and Salted Duck Egg with Courgette, and especially the Massaman Bavette, which was the standout dish.

The service was great, the food was amazing, and the restaurant has a lovely atmosphere. The open kitchen is a nice touch too - you can watch the chefs at work while you eat (if that’s your thing)

Highly recommended!

I’d recommend coming here for a drink and the chicken wings (lives up to the hype, has been on my list for years!) - crispy, salty, sweet - they balanced the flavours in such a unique way. And good value as the wings are so large (2 wings would be a meal for one person). However - the other dish we ordered was really bad imo (stir fried squid and salted duck egg). Mushy texture, over salted - and overpriced imo. So definitely worth a visit for the vibe, drinks, location and wings, but wouldn’t return for anything else tbh

Authentic street food from Bangkok. Tastes exactly like it does in Bangkok which is impressive as none of the chefs in the kitchen are Thai however they are flown there once a year to learn, the chicken wing was great however it is battered do it makes it heavy and calorific the crunch is perfect though and the sauce perfect. The fried chicken was 10/10 beautiful flavour moist perfectly cooked chicken awesome dipping sauce.
Service was fantastic and fizzy water was complimentary. Highly recommended from a private chef of 40 years and it was recommended to be by a Michelin Star ⭐ Chef.

Delicious fresh authentic Thai food. The chicken wings in a caramelised fish sauce are to die for and the langoustine curry full of lemongrass and heat. I love the atmosphere and sitting at the counter was fun. Waiting service was a bit slow but the amazing head chef saved us.

Great Thai bistro for a Friday night out. The fish source chicken is a must-have, surprisingly big for the price, the skin is so crispy and flavourful, and the meat is juicy and tender.
Love the freshly made roti, such a therapeutic thing to watch the dough is making in front of you, and all the food is made in the open kitchen.
The Tom Yum pork noodles is great but a bit overly salty for me.

Restaurant is a bit tight but good vibe, considering it's in Shoreditch, that's the vibe you would go for. Definitely will come back again for those chicken wings.

name: Teparos Thai Street Food
address: The Brown Bear Pub, 139 Leman St, London E1 8EY, UK

reviews.text: Been there a couple times since it opened. Absolutely love this place! One of my favourite Thai restaurants in London! The food was delicious. Lovely staff, friendly chef, sometimes he comes out from the kitchen to say hi. Definitely want to support the business 👍👍
Absolutely loved this place! Super authentic Thai food at a low price, especially yum fried pork belly and yum kanom jeen!

I’m Thai. This is the very AUTHENTIC Thai food in London. I’ve tried crispy pork with rice and it is the best! It is very crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Everything is really nice. The lunch set is very cheap when compared to other restaurants. I miss Thailand and I will come back to this place for sure!
Hidden gems of Thai food in London. You will find all unexpected menu that you think it could only be found in Thailand! Super tasty 👍🏻

What a hidden gem! Loved the chef's service and dishes. Must to order the Panang Curry.
Full review available at my food blog.

I am from NYC and have had my fair share of Thai food and US customer service, something Europe does lack. Abul, the owner started "Hungry Lane" about 1.5 years ago. Hungry Lane consists of a few restaurants, Thai Lane, Brick Boi Burger, and two others. We didn't immediately see a storefront so we called the owner and he set us up with a table and chairs in the shop he shares. Before the owner got there, Monair, one of the workers (so kind, by the way--his smile brightened our night), set us up with salt and pepper chips. The chips were excellent. It was my first time having chips in this manner
Both Monair and Abul did their very best to make us feel at home. They were honest, jovial and welcoming. The Panang Curry was perfect with the Jasmine Rice. The Pad Kee Mao was spicy and they gave a great bit of beef. The Pad Thai had extra chicken and a hint of spice. What a nice surprise! I loved the hospitality and the food. Abul made us feel at home. I recommend this place to everyone!

I recently ordered takeaway from this spot, and it was a great experience overall. The packaging was clean, sturdy, and kept everything hot without getting soggy. The flavors were fresh and well-balanced — especially the main dish, which arrived perfectly seasoned and still steaming. Portions were generous, and nothing felt rushed or thrown together.

Delivery was on time, and the food looked just as good as it tastes in the restaurant. For anyone craving quality takeaway that doesn’t lose its charm on the way home, this place is definitely worth it.

Had a great dine-in experience with friends. The place had a lovely vibe, and the staff - especially the guy who served us was super friendly and attentive. We really enjoyed the food overall, everything was delicious and well-prepared. Just one small thing - one of the noodle dishes had a bit too much turmeric. Apart from that, everything was spot on. Definitely coming back!

I ordered the salt and pepper fries, which I get regularly, and as always, they were delicious. The food was fresh, full of flavour, and consistently good. Abul took care of us, providing the same great service he always does—attentive, friendly, and making sure everything was just right. Always a reliable spot for both tasty food and excellent service.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 Stars
I ordered from Thai Lane through Uber Eats and was so impressed! The food arrived quickly and was still hot and fresh. The flavors were amazing — perfectly balanced, rich, and authentic. The Pad Thai had just the right amount of sweetness and spice, and the Green Curry was creamy and full of tender vegetables and chicken. Portion sizes were generous, and everything was packed neatly so nothing spilled during delivery.

If you’re craving Thai food, this place is definitely worth it. Delicious, fresh, and great quality for the price — I’ll be ordering again soon!

name: Satay Street BOXPARK Shoreditch
address: Satay Street Unit 56 2-10 Bethnal Green Rd Boxpark, London E1 6GY, UK

reviews.text: Isor makes the best Pad Thai and green curry I’ve had. Everything was packed with flavour, perfectly balanced, and you can tell it’s made with real care and skill. The service was just as good as the food warm, attentive, and made the whole experience feel effortless. You’re looked after from start to finish. If you’re into proper Thai food done right, this is it. Would 100 percent come back again. Thank you

I got the £10 lunch meal (12pm - 3pm) this came with one main and one drink - the portion was perfect very filling, I got the chicken pad Thai, loved the rich flavour. (On the right side of the picture)
My bf got the chicken green curry, he got a regular meal. The curry is very delicious, I would say though that there’s more vegetables than the actual chicken but nevertheless it was still very tasty! We didn’t really wait so the food was still very hot which is nice!

The man who served me tonight was so lovely! I ordered the stir-fried chilli and basil chicken & it was absolutely delicious. I asked for it to be spicier and he made it perfectly. It tasted truly authentic and full of flavour. Highly recommend it!

This is great high quality Thai food for a very reasonable price and the quantities are amazing! I love the Thai green chicken curry with rice (and free beverage) lunch meal deal- I literally feel so full after eating it and it has a good amount of chicken and vegetables in it as well. Sometimes service can be a little slow but I think it’s worth the wait!
There are only box park benches to sit on which aren’t super comfortable but good enough for a quick meal. There’s also heating in the winter time so that’s nice.

I ordered a vegetarian meal
Luckily I eat meat, my sister does not. I ordered a vegetarian dumplings with our meal and bit into one. Chicken! Returned the meal and they promised the replacement meal was vegetarian. She bit into a new dumpling and it was also chicken. Total.disregard for vegetarians, I would never order again.

I came by for a quick weekend dinner around 7pm -- lots of tables still available (very spacious, roughly half full). I ordered the Nam Tok (five spice) noodle soup, which I think is basically Thai boat noodles. The broth had a wonderfully rich aroma (savoury and dark pork blood flavour) and the braised beef was so tender and flavourful. The noodles were a perfect chewiness and carried the broth flavour very well.

Service was prompt, friendly, and helpful, and the price point was fantastic for the quality and portion size of my dish. I'd love to visit again to try some of their other yummy dishes. They also have a lovely bar space in the basement that I saw on the way to the washroom -- would love to give it a try someday as well.

As I person who eats Thai food almost daily... this restaurant is an absolute must if wanting authentic street/home style Thai food.....Food was of excellent quality and served promptly.. staff were super helpful and supportive over trying to decide NOT to eat the entire menu.. come here 10/10

WOAH!!

I am so impressed!

Slurp serves up super tasty Thai noodle soups and so much more.

From the Five Spice Noodle Soup, loaded with a rich spiced pork broth and rice noodles to the Sen Su Koh Thai Soup,
a marriage of tangy, spicy, sweet and salty flavors with roast pork, dried shrimp & fishballs, every dish was loaded with bursts of deliciousness!

The papaya salad was a bit too spicy but I simply washed it down with a homemade Thai iced tea. Yum. 😋

I will absolutely return to this explore more of this menu!!

Thai Restaurant

Went to the Soutalfields Market therefore have lunch here.

The food was in moderate portions.  Not too large or too small.  Both soup noodles tasted nice without disappointment.

Unfortunately the starters were a bit let down.  The fried chicken thighs and chive cakes (they looked like chocolate brownie)were too dry.  I need to dip them into my noodle soup to finish.

At least the environment and toilet were nice, clean and quiet.  The staff were nice and friendly.  Prices were reasonable for London.

The food is delicious. I highly recommend the Sukhothai Noodles, which truly taste as if they came directly from Sukhothai.
The restaurant offers a wide variety of Thai dishes such as Pad Mi Korat, Pad Krapow (Basil Stir-fry), Pad Thai, and Boat Noodles (Kuay Teow Reua).
The restaurant is clean, and I suggest making a reservation in advance

We visited the restaurant on a Sunday afternoon.
We were welcomed and seated by a lovely lady.
The restaurant wasn’t busy at all time we got there.
We ordered a sharing platter which was a great idea as we got to try few things instead of ordering one side.
For the mains we had tofu pad Thai and chicken pad Thai.
Both were very delicious, full of flavour.
My partner who usually doesn’t eat Asian food and is not a big foodie really liked it so it must have been good.
My tofu one was great too and the portion size was generous.
The prices are very reasonable too.
We both had drinks, I had a Thai tea with condensed milk.
The service was very nice especially the lady with a pony tail who welcomed us and a guy who came later. He was very friendly, polite and helpful. He looked after the customers and made sure everyone is happy, they deserve a recognition.
I can recommend this place.
Thank You!

Delicious! We went for dinner with some friends, and it was easily some of the best Thai food I’ve ever had. The fried calamari were outstanding, and my Pad Thai was absolutely delicious. Just a heads-up—the green curry was a bit on the spicy side for some in our group, so be prepared for a kick! 🌶️🍚 I would highly recommend this place to anyone craving authentic Thai cuisine.

Overall I’ve given it 4 stars but it’s more like 4.5. The food was lovely I got the flat noodles with chicken and a lemon ice tea no milk. The ice tea was a little bitter for my liking but it went quite well with the noodles as they were on the sweeter side. And the chicken was a tad bit dry but otherwise the meal was good. The atmosphere was actually lovely very warm, artsy feel and good music, the only thing was the seating wasn’t very comfortable. It’s good for a quick meal so I would probably go back for lunch again as overall it was a pleasant experience.
I tried the Pad Kra Prow and Thai milk tea — both were amazing! The stir-fry had the perfect balance of spice and basil, and the milk tea was creamy and refreshing. Highly recommend!
Amazing food! We took a second portion because it was too good! Atmosphere very friendly! They even speak italian (like me)! Grazie! Everything delicious ♥️

Great little find.
Very decent food for good prices.
Had sushi and my favourite was the prawn katsu temaki, really wonderful.

Service was quick and attentive. Can't ask for much more overall.

Fantastic restaurant with thai and japanese food. The prices are really cheap for London. The food is fantastic and authentic. We had some Satay, Gyozas and a Mussaman Curry (with fried rice). The Satay were authentic as well as the Gyozas. The curry was one of the best Mussaman curries I ever had - even better than most I had in southern Thailand. The Pad Thai is also good - it was a bit on the sweeter site with lots of tamarind.
The staff is very nice and the drinks are served fast, are presented in nice glasses and are very affordable. My recommendation: try the ginger beer.
Would visit brick lane again just for another dinner there.

We visited Enso Lounge on Brick Lane and shared fried gyoza, crab sushi, sirloin and beef fried rice. The crab sushi and sirloin really stood out, while the gyoza were crisp and the fried rice was flavorful. The service was really good and attentive throughout. We found the restaurant via The Fork — highly recommend using their discount.

We decided to try this place out with a special offer from TheFork, and we were so glad we did! The servers were friendly and made us feel right at home. We really enjoyed the food and service.

The Dragon Rolls were a total showstopper—we were so impressed we ordered them twice! The Pad Thai was absolutely perfect, hitting all the right notes. While the fried chicken gyoza was a little bland and the Weeping Tiger beef was a bit overcooked, it wasn't enough to spoil the meal.

I'd definitely recommend this restaurant and will happily return in the future.

This restaurant serves cheap large portions of not so authentic Thai and Japanese food.  Good flavours.  Textures and details not always right.

We wanted to try a nori roll to start.  For a restaurant that purports to serve Japanese, there are few items containing raw fish on the menu.  That in itself is not terrible, because not stocking perishible ingredients keeps prices down.  We opted for the california maki roll containing deep fried soft shelled crab.  It was a good roll where sushi rice was at the correct temperature (not fridge cold), the nori and fried crab were crisp.  Also rolls were dotted rather than drenched in mayo.  My only criticism was rice was packed a little too dense so didn't fall into loose grains on the palate, but that is a picky detail.

The rest of our Thai order came with more misgivings.  The person who designed the menu and recipes knew what they were doing in terms of balancing Thai flavours of salty, sweet, sour and hot.  However, textures were often wrong and corners were cut in terms of either techniques and ingredients.  I missed, for example, herbal notes of coriander and/or mint in the Thai dishes.

First to arrive was Som Tam.  Positives were flavour balance, crunchiness of vegetables, and a little mound of chopped peanuts to use as garnish.  What diminished the dish was the use of a sticky sweet commercial chilli sauce in the dressing which made it too thick, so too much sauce clung to the veg.  This version of som tam seemed to lack garlic and dried shrimp.

My main of Weeping Tiger steak was okay.  The dipping sauce (which also is used as marinade) was good only very slightly sweet.  I couldn't taste the funk of fish sauce, so proportions must have been weighted towards soy sauce.  Steak should have been seared at high heat and served plain with the dipping sauce on the side.  It arrived tossed in the sauce, maybe in even wokked with charred vegetables. Thankfully it was still medium rare.  Big portion.

My companion's fried rice dish of Kao Pad with chicken was flavourful and generous.  It contained the funk of dried shrimp which I really liked.  However, the wet texture was a bit of a let down.  For a good texture, fried rice should be made with rice that has completely cooled after cooking.  I don't believe this was the case.  Also the wok temperature may have been too low.  Very big portion.

The red house wine was not great but good value for £25 a bottle.

In general, Enso is a good spot for an inexpensive hearty meal if you are not expecting authenticity.  They do a decent approximation of Thai and Japanese food.

name: Thai n Pie Stepney
address: 45 Mile End Rd, Bethnal Green, London E1 4TT, UK

reviews.text: The Ribeye and T-bone. Ordered medium well. Was tasty and juicy. Could have more flavour if I’m being honest and could’ve been a little more done. Overall was nice. Chips were fluffy and nice. Service was great. Waiters were amazing. It is a quiet cosy place itself. You could see the chefs cooking from the dining area. 7/10 i would give go overall experience.

After moving to the UK, this used to be one of my favourite places. I went there almost every week. As you can see from the post I shared three years ago, I really loved it back then. Unfortunately, the place has changed a lot. Today I ordered Pad Thai, and it didn’t taste the same at all  the flavour was disappointing, and they didn’t even include peanuts. The staff have changed too, and the service wasn’t good. It’s sad to say, but we won’t be going there anymore. 😞

The food here is very delicious and authentically Thai. I will definitely come again!

Surprisingly, the chef is Bangladeshi, but the taste is so good I honestly thought it was a Thai chef.

Kudos to the team!
Its a okay place.  They have tried there best to provide a good service.  Food was ok but can do with more flavour specially grill items.  Thai menu was tasty.

We hired the space downstairs for a 60th birthday and couldn’t be happier with the service we received. The room for 45 people comfortably. The food was so delicious and well priced. Staff were very accommodating and we all felt very relaxed under their care. Ahmed and his team were fantastic ahead of the day and on the day. Could not recommend them enough.

My friend and I  had the best time at Rosa’s Thai on Tuesday evening 13/01/26.
The atmosphere was great.
Can’t compliment my food enough as it was just amazing.
I was torn between pad Thai and a curry but eventually I went for the tofu pad Thai and it was a great choice.
It was full of flavour, hot and portion was generous.
I also ordered the veggie summer rolls on the side and I didn’t realise they will be cold but it is my fault not checking with a staff member before ordering.
The staff was very helpful and friendly.
The lady serving us was kind and very polite, we had a nice chat.
I also had a tea with a condensed milk, and I asked to make it less sweet as I knew it will be very sweet.
Great experience!
One of the best meals I had in a long time!
I will be back to try more options!
I recommend this place!
If you haven’t been there yet, plan your visit!
Thanks !

Me and my wife went here before going cinema one night, didn’t make a booking but didn’t have to wait for a table.

Staff were extremely helpful and attentive all of them asking if we needed anything.

Nice relaxed atmosphere inside.

Food was lovely especially the sweetcorn fritters and massaman beef curry.

Only criticism I can make was that my egg fried rice didn’t arrive until I had nearly finished my main so ended taking some of my wife’s rice. However they took the egg fried rice off the bill at the end.

Overall had a lovely meal, I would go back here.

Place had a great atmosphere. Food was great and service by Meen was really good.
Ordered the unlimited curries which gave a chance to sample different curries.

Recently had dinner here and had a great experience. My friends and I ordered an array of items, all of which tasted amazing. We were served by the lovely Mirelle who took the time to explain new menu items that we might enjoy, such as the stir fried cabbage and morning glory. Give her a raise ;)

Would 11/10 come again!

Ps. Unexpectedly, I loved the deep fried kale.

I have visited this thai restaurant today. The food i ate was Pad thai chicken, crispy pork, papaya salad and beef salad all the dish was amazing and tasty. I recommend other to visit here and taste the flavour of thai food. It was really busy but they managed to give our order quickly.The service given Aof and meen were amazing. Top notch hospility. Thank you so much for your good service ❤️❤️❤️

Overall, fantastic authentic Thai food. Having lived in Chiang Mai for 7 years, this is the closest I have had to real Thai food outside of Thailand. Location is a few footsteps from London Fields Station. Small branch with only 8 tables or so. Staff all polite and helpful but unfortunately understaffed. Only 2 slight negatives, kitchen is right by the tables so you will leave smelling of food, not a real issue, and quite pricey. Albeit the portions are huge, and I mean huge, our meal cost £93 for 2. Prawn crackers were delicious, very large portion and realistically enough for 4 person as a light starter snack. Satay was ok, but not exceptional. Thai squid was delicious, light batter with a salt/pepper/chilli coat, a must get starter. Pad Thai portion was huge! It only comes as a main meal, would be ideal if there was a small side plate version but absolutely delicious nonetheless. Penang curry was also fantastic and also the morning glory is another must order (although the leaf from the vegetable was removed which is the best part). Star of the show for me was the Thai holy Basil pork belly, exceptional taste, and spicy as it should be!! Although the pork belly would be crispy when ordered in Thailand, the meat was incredibly soft so it was just as good. Overall I would recommend Rosa’s however, do not over order ad the portions are huge and the bill will also be the same!!

good food and friendly service. drinks were great too (the lychee spritz is amazing).
it was SO cold inside the restaurant tho :(

Got the lunch special today and my taste buds exploded with all the flavors! 🤯😍✨ Incredible food, great and very friendly service and although the dip sauce for the corn fritters is apparently not listed in their cookbook (secret recipe 😭) I will buy it! 😁
Highly recommend you come here and taste your way through the menu!
I‘ll definitely be back soon 🤩🙏

I placed an order and what arrived was an absolute mess. The curry containers leaked badly, soaking through the paper bags and dripping everywhere (on my hands, the floor, and the kitchen counter). The bag was so drenched it was falling apart at the bottom from the moment the delivery guy wanted to hand it over to me.

What’s frustrating is the complete lack of thought that went into the packaging. You don’t pack food for delivery the same way you do for someone picking it up and going for a stroll. Delivery requires extra care: sturdier packaging, double-bagging, leak-proof containers, or at least a protective layer to contain any spills. None of that was done here.

To the store manager: I’m upset by this experience! You’ve failed big time, shown carelessness and a disregard for how food traveled from your kitchen to me as your customer. I spent so much time cleaning up my kitchen and the hallway, whilst trying to save as much food as possible. As such, I lost appetite because it’s hard to enjoy a meal when it arrives in such chaos. I won’t trust your place ever again!

A real gem!

Situated in the railway arches under London Fields station this place was a great find.

The humble surroundings hide a fantastic kitchen which serves up authentic Thai dishes served hot and fast.

We decided immediately on leaving that we are going back in the next few days....

I recently dined at Thai Square Minories and had a thoroughly enjoyable experience. The restaurant strikes a lovely balance between elegance and comfort, with romantic décor, warm lighting and a calm atmosphere that makes it ideal for date nights or special occasions.

We started with a refreshing selection of drinks, including lychee juice and a vibrant mocktail, which set the tone nicely. Starters such as butterfly prawns and duck spring rolls were well executed, crisp, flavourful and not overly heavy. The highlight of the meal was the caramelised seabass with lemongrass, delicately cooked and beautifully balanced, paired with fragrant coconut and sticky rice.

Dessert offered a relaxed finish, from indulgent chocolate pudding with vanilla ice cream to lighter coconut and mango ice creams. Service throughout the evening was attentive without being intrusive, and the pacing of the meal felt unhurried.

Overall, Thai Square Minories delivers refined Thai comfort food in a welcoming, romantic setting. A dependable choice in the City, particularly for those looking for a polished yet relaxed dining experience.

I recently visited Thai Square Minories with my family, and it proved to be an excellent choice for a relaxed yet memorable meal in central London. This striking Thai restaurant sits just a short walk from the Tower of London, making the location ideal for visitors, business meetings, or family dinners. Thai Square Minories has been part of the London dining scene for over 20 years, and that experience shows in both the food and the service.

From the moment you step inside, the scale of the venue stands out. The restaurant is large, spacious, and beautifully decorated with traditional Thai touches that feel warm rather than overwhelming. It works well for families, as there is plenty of room and a calm atmosphere, but it also suits professional lunches and group dinners. You never feel rushed, which adds to the overall enjoyment.

We began with prawn crackers served with a sweet chilli sauce. Light, crisp, and fresh, they set a pleasant tone. The Thai dumplings followed and were a highlight among the starters. These steamed parcels were filled with chicken and prawns, along with shiitake mushrooms and water chestnuts. The topping of crispy garlic flakes added texture, while the sweet soya sauce brought everything together. They were well-balanced and full of flavour.

The chicken satay was another solid choice. Chargrilled marinated chicken breast arrived on skewers, tender and juicy, with a rich peanut sauce that tasted freshly made rather than overly sweet. Alongside this, we tried the butterfly prawns. These king prawns were coated in crispy soya breadcrumbs and served with sweet chilli sauce. They were crunchy on the outside, succulent inside, and very moreish.

Thai Square is known for its signature dishes, and they are not to be missed. The caramelised sea bass with lemongrass was outstanding. A whole sea bass, lightly coated in a crisp batter, arrived perfectly cooked and topped with fragrant herbs. The chilli jam added depth without overpowering the fish. This dish alone is reason enough to visit. Equally impressive was the chilli spider soft shell crab. Fried in a light, crispy batter and tossed with chillies and spring onions, it delivered bold flavour with a satisfying crunch.

For mains, we shared a range of classic dishes. The pad si ew was packed with flavour. Flat rice noodles were stir-fried with chicken, egg, broccoli, carrots, and cabbage in dark soya sauce with white pepper. It was comforting, rich, and very well executed.

The green curry chicken was aromatic and well-balanced, with green chilli paste, coconut milk, aubergines, bamboo shoots, long beans, and sweet basil. It had warmth without being overpowering.

The panang curry chicken offered a creamier option, with a thicker red curry sauce, coconut milk, bell peppers, and shredded lime leaves. It was deeply flavoured and satisfying.

We finished with mango sticky rice, which was in season. Sweet, ripe mango was paired with soft sticky rice, topped with coconut sauce and sesame seeds. There was a subtle pandan note that lifted the dessert and ended the meal on a high.

Service deserves special praise. Sonia looked after us throughout the meal and made excellent recommendations. She was attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable. The rest of the team was equally professional and welcoming, going above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable.

Thai Square Minories delivers authentic Thai cuisine in a beautiful setting. With several branches across London, this location stands out for its size, atmosphere, and consistent quality. It is a place you can return to with confidence, whether dining with family, friends, or colleagues.

Halal chicken is available.

Incredibly authentic and tasty Thai food. Truly delicious! The service is always very friendly and professional. Sonja and colleagues are simply wonderful. Very reasonable prices too for the quality provided. It is also a really beautiful space with lots of interesting art. Recommended!
Very nice restaurant and service. Food was very good just a little bit to less. The sticky rice dessert was green :) We just arrived with the plane, checked-in at motel one and were tired and hungry.

The food was well done. If you like thai food then go for it. Personally I only like a couple dishes and I didn't like the tamarind duck. It was too sweet and too many flavours all competing. However the staff were nice and attentive and my vegan friend liked the food. Its quite big inside with a relaxed atmosphere. There were a lot of single diners in there so don't be shy about it. It's also a good place for a group meal if you like thai food.

name: Singburi
address: Unit 7, Montacute Yards, 185‑186 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6HU, UK

reviews.text:
Had a great lunch at Singburi, though it was a bit of a mixed bag. Starting with drinks, the updated Cox Daiquiri was fantastic—so good I ordered a second!

The small plates were the real winners for us. The grilled chicken was perfectly cooked, so yummy and succulent with great subtle flavors, we had to get seconds of that one. The mains like the aubergine and the cabbage were also very nice; the cabbage was crunchy and flavourful, and the aubergine was a tasty way to get some veg in.

However, a couple of dishes were disappointing. The lamb riblets, while extremely tasty and nicely cooked (I even asked for some of the sauce for my other dishes!), were way too fatty and didn't have enough actual lamb meat, which was a shame. And the pork curry just wasn't to my taste; the pork seemed a bit separate and didn't feel like it had absorbed any of the curry flavour.

The service, though, was excellent! The staff were great, taking their time to answer all our questions about the menu and giving genuinely helpful recommendations.

Overall, it was a really good lunch, but I was definitely disappointed by the fatty lamb and the underwhelming pork curry.

Singburi was 11/10 magnificent. Lovely and super well informed service, our waiter gave so many terrific recommendations. INCREDIBLE food. Honestly guys. The aubergine pad phet is easily one of the best dishes I’ve had this year. A masterpiece of texture and flavour. Will be dreaming of it forever more. £160 altogether for 2 people, ordered (almost) every dish under the sun, a delightful Paloma each, and a lovely bottle of wine too. Well worth it!

Singburi is overhyped. Service was okay. Food portions are tiny as others have already mentioned and the atmosphere is lacking - they need a live dj or something to improve the vibe. I went on a Sunday night.

The food itself - I was in a group of 3 and we ordered : grilled chicken thigh x2, grilled lamb (we sent it back because it was just grilled lamb fat so it was inedible), stir fried morning glory x1, grilled fish, aubergine pad phet, beef curry and jasmine rice with drinks. The bill was around 130£ with service. The best out of what we ordered was the grilled fish, chicken thigh and morning glory.

The flavours of the food were overly salty and not spicy at all. Also, they brought out the salty meat dishes out one by one and had to ask for the rice to come out. I was confused because I thought the rice would come out with the meat dishes.

I wouldn't return and I would not recommend.  There is nothing outstanding on the menu. I have spent £15 at my local Thai restaurant and had more food and more flavours.

Singburi has brought its legendary Thai flavours to Shoreditch and absolutely delivers.

The smoked pork belly (nam dtok) and wild ginger chicken are knockout dishes, juicy and full of authentic spice.

The vibe is cool yet welcoming with its remarkable hospitality. Great cocktails and a smart wine list to match all dishes. A cult classic reborn and is better than ever. Highly recommend!!!

I had been eagerly looking forward to visiting Singburi, especially after hearing so much praise for their original location in Walthamstow. The new spot did not disappoint.

The restaurant features a long, open counter where you can watch the team in action — both in the kitchen and behind the bar crafting cocktails. The space is bright, airy, and inviting, with a laid-back but vibrant atmosphere.

From the moment we walked in, the staff made us feel completely at home. Our waitress was exceptionally friendly and wore a constant, genuine smile. She guided us through the menu with confidence and clarity, which helped us get the most out of the experience.

The food? Outstanding. Every dish delivered bold, layered flavours that stayed with us long after the meal. We shared four starters and three mains between the two of us — a perfect amount for exploring the menu without going overboard.

Highlights included the dill pork sausage and the smoked pork nam, both deeply savoury and satisfying. The salads, however, truly stole the show: the watermelon and strawberry salad was refreshing and full of contrast, while the smoked tomato salad was a masterclass in balance and depth.

Sungburi lives up to the hype — and then some. We’ll definitely be coming back.
The best Thai restaurant in London! Food was amazing, staff were super kind, and the food came out really fast. Last but not least, the bathroom was extremely clean. Highly recommend!

Really happy with the flavours of the panang chicken curry. It gets pretty crowded at lunch time. We came just after 12 and managed to get a table for 2. I'd definitely come back for the £10.95 lunch special.

The staff downstairs in the pub were friendly too.

Lovely little Thai restaurant above a pub. We were welcomed by friendly attentive staff who fortunately found us a table in a popular and lively dining room. The carefully presented food tasted not as good as it looked, but the meal was still tasty enough. Good prices and a nice atmosphere made for an all round enjoyable experience.

As a Thai, I must say this is one of the best Thai restaurants I’ve tried in London. The flavors are so authentic, just like back home! The prices are reasonable, and the portions are very generous. I ordered the Thai BBQ pork set for two, and we could barely finish it because it was so filling. They even have Som Tum with fermented crab and fish sauce, which is a rare find here. Absolutely worth the price! If you’re craving authentic Thai food in London, I highly recommend this place.

This restaurant is upstairs in the Three Cranes Pub. The first floor has seating for just over 20 people, it can get quite busy, so get there early. You can take your drinks from the pub upstairs to the restaurant or you can order from upstairs too.
The food is very good. The wings are spicy and tasty, I recommend you try them. They have a lunch menu of a starter and main for less than £15 which is excellent value. The service is excellent, and yet they don't charge for it. Please take some cash for the staff if you are a large party. So good that I will be visiting on a regular basis.

name: Bangkok Bites (Shoreditch)
address: 147 Bethnal Grn Rd, London E2 7DG, UK

reviews.text:
Dinner at Bangkok Bites Shoreditch 🍣✨

If you’re going, here’s what I’d 100% recommend:

⭐ Pad Thai with Beef – proper wok flavour, savoury, slightly sweet, super comforting.
⭐ Green Curry Seafood – rich, creamy, and fragrant with just the right level of spice.
⭐ Tom Kha Soup – light coconut broth with a fresh tangy kick… so soothing.

Also tried: rainbow roll + chicken katsu curry (both solid choices 👌)

Such a good spot for a casual Shoreditch dinner with friends 🤍

What a truly wonderful place to eat! From the moment we arrived, we were made to feel welcome and completely at ease. The food was absolutely outstanding — beautifully presented, full of flavor, and clearly prepared with great care and attention to detail. Every dish we tried exceeded our expectations.
The staff were incredibly accommodating, warm, and genuinely lovely. Nothing was too much trouble, and they went above and beyond to ensure we had everything we needed.
A special mention must go to the owner, who made a real effort to personally check in on us and ensure we were well looked after. That personal touch made the whole experience feel even more special and memorable.
We will definitely be returning and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for exceptional food.
I really enjoy Bangkok Bite. I usually order their noodles and they never disappoint. Fresh, full of flavour, and always satisfying. Definitely one of my go-to food spots.

Bangkok Bites (Shoreditch) served absolutely delicious food with bold and authentic flavors. Every dish was fresh, beautifully presented, and perfectly balanced in taste. The service was friendly and attentive, making the overall experience outstanding. Highly recommended for anyone looking for amazing Thai cuisine. I will definitely be coming back!

I ordered pad thai and a green curry. The pad thai had a nice balance of sweet and savory, with plenty of noodles and fresh toppings. It wasn’t overly saucy, which I liked, and the portion size was generous. The green curry had a good level of spice — enough heat to notice, but not so much that it overpowered everything. The chicken was tender, and the vegetables still had some bite to them.

Everything tasted fresh, and the flavors felt authentic without being overwhelming. Service was friendly and the food came out quickly.

Overall, it’s a solid restaurant with good portions and fair prices. I’d definitely go back when I’m craving Thai food.

I ordered the Veg Gyozas and the Pad Thai wih prawns (without peanuts because I'm intolerant). Both were very good, in fact I ended up ordering another Pad Thai! The prices are a bit high (£12.45 for the Pad Thai, not a small portion but not a big one either), but considering the city area they're in, they could be a lot higher; the food is good and the staff is friendly so it's worth the money!
Lovely pad Thai ! We added some chilli oil to ours and it was great 😍

The most amazing food I have tried in the market. Slowly going through the menu and nothing disappoints, everything is so lovely!

Definitely try this if you are a fan of Thai food!

This place shouldn't even exist or be open. Both the food and service were sad. I ordered a pad Thai which was drenched in sugary sauce and had three strips of chicken. It initially came without the peanuts (which was part of the dish) and I had to ask for it. No veggies either. Just sharing so you avoid the disappointment.

I had an amazing experience at Ithaca this morning. I ordered the pad Thai chicken and grapow chicken I must say the food was full of flavor delicious and the portions were generous. Sayana and Dayz were very friendly and attentive without being overbearing. The place was clean, well lit and had a cosy vibe with background music also prices were fair for the quality and quantity of food. Highly recommended make sure everyone visits.

I had such a wonderful experience at Rabieng! The service was exceptionally warm and attentive, making us feel truly welcome. The food was absolutely delicious — every dish was packed with authentic Thai flavors, just like in Thailand. A perfect spot for anyone looking for genuine Thai cuisine. Highly recommended!

came here on a first table of the green curry duck was solid whilst the ducks tasted like cha siew and the the Thai iced tea was bombed. I had the Thai lemon tea which was like a yacult so kind of interesting and had the shrimp laksa and which was on the sweet side like a Tom, yum so definitely stick to the Thai things but overall pretty decent

Mark and the team at Rabieng are such kind and thoughtful people who have many attributes one in common and one of those attributes is to provide a pleasant and satisfying dining experience.. 🙏🏿
Been dining there for well over 10 years now and every time the level of care and attention is exemplary.
Recommend Rabieng Thai Restaurant to all those who love Thai food and if you don't, try it anyway.  You won't be disappointed.
Mel...😇😇
Well don

Such a lovely restaurant! Absolutely fantastic service, our lovely waiter was very friendly and attentive, including bringing tap water unprompted and regularly refilling our water glasses which was very appreciated. Great music and decor contributed to a peaceful vibe. The food was good and we particularly loved the drinks - we had a Thai iced milk tea and a fresh lemonade which were flavourful and delicious. A great spot on Upper Street!

I was so stoked to see that Rabieng was available on First Table! It’s a local Thai restaurant that I discovered a few months ago and really loved. Went there twice with different groups of friends and everyone was unanimous: delicious food, super attentive staff and reasonable prices. So what’s not to like when you can eat there with an extra 50% off? Honestly there’s no catch, it’s just one of these rare good deals in London. I’ll definitely keep using the app when I need a Thai food fix!

Had an excellent meal. Ordered Pad Thai Prawns with crustaceans, egg and peanuts. With a quash piece on lemon on the noodles and the chilli flakes, worked wonders. Was excellent choice and tasted amazing.

Such a cute place to enjoy authentic Thai food. The owner and their chef are Thai. Their Signature Bao Bun Chicken Satay & Beef Massaman, Pad Thai with prawns are my favourite.  Bao bun is quite similar to steamed pork in Vietnam cuisine with meat and satay sauce inside. crispy, tender chicken, and a creamy satay sauce. They have 2 locations: 1 food stall in Petticoat Lane and the other is this cafe restaurant. Highly recommend!!

If you're looking for spice and great food this is the place! Bar height seating inside and a few cafe style tables outside. The interior is a bit lacking, better to take away or eat out front. Stir-fry with chili and basil is SO good, you can control the spice level. Chicken Satay is good however a bit too sweet for my taste. They do not have Thai Iced Tea. The staff is very nice. Highly recommended.

Reasonable price. The Best tofu Satay in town. The peanut sauce was so AMAZING & JUICY serving with rice & pickle salad on side. The chicken Satay wrap was also super delicious!
We really enjoy our lunch break :))) Highly recommended!!!

One of the best lunch spots for a hearty and delicious satay chicken and rice! Always go for the large even though the standard portion is pretty hefty. The pickles are amazing and the rice is always perfectly cooked. I get it at least once a week and the staff are always friendly! Highly recommended!
Absolutely delicious and best takeaway I think I’ve ever had! Great value Meal for 2, chicken green curry and lamb massaman curry were both fantastic!!

Don’t order takeaway from here if you are vegetarian. Twice now they have put meat/fish into my order. The first time they sent out a new order when I called, but the second time their phone line was dead so I could do nothing about it. Really disappointing

A must try for all food lovers. We regularly use them for office events. Their lunch boxes are a major hit which we order for all the staff in the office (over a hundred people) and it never disappoints.
The masaman curry and the Singapore fried rice was an excellent mixof flavours. The chef is really good I must say. Delivery was prompt aswell got it in 20 mins.
The veg and tofu pad Thai had one single piece of tofu in it. Portion size is so much smaller than I used to get. Not worth it, get your pad Thai elsewhere.

Great tasting street food served indoors, super quick, generous portions, friendly staff/family run vibe.
I had the vegetable tofu red curry.
Very decent soup. Unfortunately I had to eat it in the company or people working on Worship street

Delicious Pad Thai at a great price! Perfect for a quick grab-and-go, but there are also a few seats if you want to sit and enjoy your lunch. Super friendly Thai staff 🌟🌟🌟 Definitely coming back to try more dishes!

Note: It doesn’t come with chili powder by default, but I’d recommend adding a bit if you like some extra flavour! 🌶️

Amazing thai food in town. Vegan meat ball with curry is my favorite. It tasted is same as my mom cooked for me when i was young. Salt and pepper squid is mvp of the meal. It’s crispy but inside is soft and fresh. It make me want to quit being vegan. Highly recommended.

I got the chicken satay and rice from the market stall on Klifton Street London, though unfortunately the chicken was very raw and I didn’t notice until I had eaten a good portion. Thankfully I returned with it and was granted a refund, but I unfortunately needed to push for a refund as I declined their insistence to remake the dish as I felt very ill at the thought. Then they tried to suggest £7.95, while I’d paid £9.95 total which included a chicken side to which I also then had to stop eating. After pushing, I was refunded - though it appeared to have the intent of stopping a scene instead of because they thought it was the right thing to do. Chicken is the worst thing to undercook and leave raw, which made me very worried. If I get ill in the next couple hours/days, I’ll be putting it down to food poisoning. Id have thought this chicken would have been checked, especially when cooking such a large volume at the markets. Seems like they valued quantity over quality and safety. Such a shame but never again - can’t take the risk.

I had the 8 piece duck and avocado sushi which was made fresh to order(1 clearly missing because I was eager to try😩), amazing flavours and paired well with the soy sauce & ginger. The main dish being prawn katsu curry with noodles was also amazing , it was fresh & hot and the prawns were crispy. definitely recommend😊

Awful. Ordered via deliveroo, ordered the “Vegan Pad See Lew” came with egg, ordered the “vegetable tempura” came with prawns, ordered “tofu Penang” came with no tofu. Never had a worse deliveroo experience - don’t know what’s happening in that kitchen but I’m sure it would be shut down if someone had a look inside. Blatant lack of understanding of serious allergens.
I’m not one to usually leave a review but honestly one of the worst Pad Thai noodles I have ever tried. The flavours just weren’t  there tasted very bland and off.

My experience at this restaurant was amazing the food was representative and also tasted delicious the service was very good ,the meal that I had really tasty was red curry with jasmine rice and prawn satay. I recommend you to try out the origin Thai restaurant.
This restaurant is fantastic for takeout or dining in. Top Indian food, It would be well worth your while to visit this place as well.

name: Thai Square Mansion House
address: 1 Great St Thomas Apostle, London EC4V 2BH, UK

reviews.text: Lovely Thai restaurant. The food was amazing and so tasty, definitely going back. Not expensive and the service was great too!

Looking forward to visit this evening along with Richard and colleagues to experience authentic Thai cuisine.

Will write a detailed review post my first visit.

Excellent venue very friendly staff. Food was delivered fast and we had a good time at Thai Square.

Loved the visit and we will visit again.

Update: came here in Jan and service was horrific, no one took our order for over half an hour even though it was quiet, the waitress spilt our wine, and our mains were luke warm. There were also buckets on the floor to catch rain water, and we were sat right next to them despite the restaurant being under half full. Not planning on coming back

Had the prawn and tofu pad Thai, the portion size was excellent and food came out very promptly. Nice vibe inside this restaurant too

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I recently visited Thai Square Mansion House for dinner and had an excellent experience. The food was of exceptional quality and absolutely delicious. While the prices may seem a bit high, I believe that’s expected given its prime location. What really stood out was the service – Ratchel, who attended to us, was incredibly efficient and provided excellent customer care. Overall, a wonderful dining experience and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for top-notch Thai food in a great location!
Very nice Thai food in the city. Very good service from the waiters, quick turn around with our orders. Was a busy evening, but we had no complaints.
Chicken Pad Thai was a decent size but a bit bland and oily. I will go back and try a green curry and amend the review if it's good.

£10.50 for a pre-made box with rice, literally 5 pieces of dry chicken and some carrots.
Just look at the depressing pic below and tell me this is authentic Thai food... Ridiculous, never going back

Had the worst pad thai here. At 10.5£ it was quite pricey, whichnwould have been justified to some extent if the food was good. The noodles were half cooked. I specifically asked for it to be cooked without any sweet sauces but it was ignored and I got noodles in a sugary syrup.

Extremely disappointed. It took nearly 30 minutes for a Chicken Pad Thai, that had very little flavour and questionable grey looking chicken. The portion size was large but unfortunately I don't think that warrants the cost when the quality and taste is poor.

It has been my favourite place for lunch since they re-open. As they said on the wall, the food is authentic and delicious! Green curry chicken rice always sold out; when I had a chance to get it, the curry seemed a bit oily and too spicy for me. But Tom Yum Noodle and Massaman Curry I have had for a few time, it tastes really good.

They had another branch near Tower Bridge, which i didn't review so it stayed a hidden gem. Unlucky for me. It shut down. So now I'm reviewing this branch, so it doesn't. Basically. It's the best Chicken Katsu I've ever had, loads of chicken, loads of sauce and all at a reasonable price. I add some soy sauce and chilli oil to taste. It's great. The staff are cool too. Decent seating. Highly recommended.

Had the tan tan ramen with chicken, the portion was great for the price so was the taste!

The food had so much depth of flavour. The servers were great and very efficient with their service.

Highly recommended!

We just needed a quick lunch before travelling back home saw this place was cheap and thought we'd try it and the food was beautiful, I hate the katsu curry which was lovely and my partner had the duck ramen which was beautiful. The broth was to die for and I'd happily drink it everyday if I could. Would highly recommend.

I quite like what they serve for lunch. Pretty decent. Good chicken karage, decent rice meal deals. But the main serving lady is a bit rushed and impatient. It really ruins the experience of trying to choose.

I was around the area and looking for quick late lunch with affordable price. And this is a hidden gem. Tastes sooooo gooooood !!!!! I got myself the prawn curry, the curry was just 🌞 🫶🫶🫶. Very decent for one person order. Definitely recommend this place.

Great food and amazing cocktails. The place is really nice, with great background music. The waitress was lovely, though it was a bit too quiet for my taste when we were there. I would have loved it to be a bit more lively.

Great food, cocktails and wine. The two of us went for a late lunch on a hot day. The dark, cozy interior felt perfect for the evening. We ordered five dishes to share plus rice, cocktails and a bottle of wine. Our waitress Vanessa was amazing – warm, friendly and so much fun to chat with. We left feeling like old friends. Thanks to Vanessa and the whole team, I will definitely be back :)

Fantastic venue, exciting cocktails and good food.
Adventurous range of vegetarian options and reasonable portion sizes - it was great to try new flavours and textures.
Avo and pickled lotus root with watermelon salad was refreshing.
The banana blossom tempura was my favourite - perfectly made with crispy batter and a zingy spicy dip.
Dessert of chocolate mousse was a bit disappointing. Very rich and needed something more to balance it out and more texture. Honeycomb was sparce and some cherry kitsch may have added more of the flavour.
Overall a great dining experience.
Excellent service. Good food! Live dj! We have been looked after by Alejandra who was truly amazing. Thank you for everything:

Nice atmosphere, but overall not worth the price. The food was fine, but nothing special, and the portions were small for what you’re paying. For £100 between two people, there are much better places in London with the same kind of vibe and better value.
We had a 90-minute time slot but after an hour and 40 minutes our dessert still hadn’t arrived and we kept having to ask for our food. The staff were clearly working hard but were understaffed, so service was very slow. The fire alarm going off during the meal didn’t help either.
Okay experience, but overpriced and forgettable.

pretty excellent selection of Japanese food for lunch, had the the rolls which were the best part. so delicious. delicious! had the spider roll along with the seared tuna and would definitely recommend that, had the black cod as well and it was cooked really really nicely except it was a sweet flavor that I didn't really expect. I guess it's just up to personal preference. anyway, I would recommend. I think overall great decent quality and especially if you get one of those first table deals

My friend and I were hungry and gave this a try without looking into the menu or reviews. We wish we had. The menu isn't anything like  what a real izakaya would do with plenty of small cooked dishes to mix and match, complemented with alcohol. Instead, most small dishes are sushi and sashimi.

Some food portions were tiny (like the few teaspoonfuls of salmon tartare for £10). 😳😬 The signature 'volcano' rolls have what I would describe as a very unconventional piled-up presentation where flavours were all mangled. One couldn't really see, let alone taste, the snow crab that's supposed to be in the rolls... 😒

The ambience was designed to be chic (dark, minimalistic), great if this is what you prefer but there's not a small hint of a Japanese izakaya. It was pretty noisy too due to the lack of soft furnishing and hard walls bouncing noises. It was hard to have a good conversation.

The service was average --- I don't think we interacted with the staff except when ordering the dishes, getting food on the table and asking do the bill. The 12.5% service charge for that 'basic' service felt excessive, but we didn't have the energy to enquire or argue.

The bill, for food and just 1 bottled water, came up to £89, that's almost £90. We could have had much a more authentic and satisfying Japanese meal elsewhere in London for the same price, if not less. It was a rather pricey but underwhelming experience overall.

Food was delicious, service was spread thin so running around constantly and had to get their attention if you needed them. Salmon tartare was outstanding. Rolls were fresh and simple. Overall would recommend

Went here for dinner on a FirstTable deal. Can’t recommend enough! Service was amazing, and food was delicious. Only took one photo!! Well worth it all, especially with a pleasant discount at the end :)

We had an amazing experience for dinner here.

The staff were exceptionally friendly, helpful, and accommodating when we called ahead to let them know we were running late for our reservation.

The menu offered a great selection of delicious dishes. We ordered several items, including fried chicken karaage, crispy squid, chicken katsu curry, and seaweed salad. However, our favorite dishes were the signature sushi rolls. I especially enjoyed the prawn tempura rolls and the vegan dragon rolls, which paired wonderfully with the fries.

The have a good tea and dessert menu too.

We have just had a delicious lunch at Tanakatsu, based in the Angel area, which was very busy at lunchtime on a Monday. The food is delicious, we had the chicken gyoza for starters and the chicken katsu curry as our main. Service is quick but unrushed, there is a great atmosphere and very busy, but thankfully we did book in advance. It is a  short walk from Angel and most customers are Japanese or Chinese which is always a great sign of authentic food. Overall the price was really good value. Highly recommended.

This is my second time to eat here for lunch. The food is absolutely delicious, fresh and flavourful. The quaint atmosphere, friendly staff and great selection is a perfect place to eat. The Bento boxes are tasty and plentiful. I have had the Katsu chicken and for vegetarian palates try the Pumpkin Croquette Curry! We tried all the starters Salmon Nigiri fresh, and complemented with a variety of Goyza’s. Can’t go wrong with anything Lon the menu. Friendly and attentive staff. I would recommend

This is honestly my favourite katsu curry spot and I'm praying that it doesn't blow up. The staff are so sweet and kind. They greet you at the door immediately and top up your water without even asking. There is also a constant check in from them if you need anything. The food is so so nice aswell and cooked to perfection. The portion sizes are HUGE not sure if anyone is ever able to finish. Thank you so much for being so kind to your customers. Special shoutout to Telma who is the kindest soul to ever exist.

The service here is excellent; staff is so friendly, making the whole meal even more enjoyable and the food is just perfect from start to finish.
The edamame are served warm and spiced with shichimi, giving them a light kick.
The miso soup with spring onion and tofu is so fresh and full of flavour, simple but done perfectly. The pumpkin croquette katsu is a must-try, crispy on the outside, soft and delicious inside, truly perfection on a plate!
Pork katsu set was divine. Not expensive, but extremely tasty. Croquettes included were really good, even the cabbage was good. Free tea to finish the meal as well!

name: SUSHINOEN
address: 2 White Church Ln, London E1 7QR, UK

reviews.text:
Sushinoen is a short walk from Aldgate East tube station, tucked into a corner building with red patterns outside. You enter via a glass door, up a few steps from the pavement, and into a fairly basic interior with a maître d’ desk at the entrance.

A Japanese movie with English subtitles plays on the wall, alongside a wooden cabinet and a red kabuki-style mask. Fake pink flowers line the top of the walls, but they feel more decorative than authentic.

Seating is arranged around a central square table that looks like it could double as a chef’s station, with more tables towards the back near the sushi counter, plus additional seating upstairs.

Food
•	Agedashi Tofu (V) – £6.95
Soft tofu with a nicely crisp batter and a good dashi sauce.
•	Takoyaki – £6.95
Five deep-fried octopus balls with brown sauce. Well cooked, and you could clearly taste the octopus tentacle.
•	Katsu Don – £15.95
Breaded pork loin on rice, topped with sweet Japanese omelette. The pork was crispy without being over-battered, and the egg was good, though there was too much rice.

The donburi overall was soft and comforting with a reasonable filling, but the ice cream dessert was average.

Drinks & Service

They offer 0% Asahi beer, and the yuzu tea was quite sweet. Service was attentive, with a 12.5% service charge added. Hiro was particularly helpful, promptly refilling water once drinks were finished.

Ambience & Comfort

The ambience is basic. There were visible stains on the walls, and the seating is very tight — so much so that Hiro had to ask diners to move so she could pass through to refill water and process payment. There’s also a noticeable lingering smell of oil on your clothes after the meal, suggesting inadequate kitchen ventilation.

Overall

Solid food and attentive service, but the cramped layout, tired décor, and ventilation issues detract from the overall experience.

The ambience was cool enough, but the food was pretty disappointing. The miso soup— delicious. The shumai— not great...not even good! It was too purely squishy and lacked flavor. Half of my sashimi was too fishy and coated with a film to enjoy as it didn’t taste fresh. The salmon and scallop (hotate) sashimis were the most fresh, but still not fresh at all compared to what I am accustomed to. The Sea Bream on my first sashimi platter was noticeably…not fresh, but I ate it anyway since I wasn’t eating the prawns or tuna due to them not being delicious and I was really hungry. When it’s fresh I love all of this stuff.

I was disappointed and had originally wanted to add more to my order but decided the quality wasn’t good enough to do so. Thankfully, when I asked for the check, they noticed I didn’t eat the tuna or prawns and brought me the freshest sea bream from today, but it was noticeably fresher than the sea bream they had served me originally. Oh— I forgot to mention that they didn’t even slice all the way through my tuna sashimi before serving it.

The servers were really nice, but they took quite a while to serve me.

I want to say this experience was mid overall, but that would be a lie. I was excited to treat myself to a nice meal, however, it was largely disappointing.

Additionally, they were out of the junmai sake I wanted but it wasn’t marked off the menu so that was also disappointing.

Really enjoyed our meal at Sushinoen.
We didn't have a reservation, but they made us feel very welcome and comfortable.  The staff are very friendly and helpful, and made some good recommendations for lunch.
The restaurant has a very pleasant atmosphere and the food was delicious and looked great.  Highly recommended.
Seated us even tho we didn't have a reservation. Incredibly nice, fast service. Beautiful decor. Sushi fabulous. Ramen might be best I've had, so perfect & delicious! Highly recommended!
Food is really delicious. Service is fast… but a little too fast. I was dining alone and they pretty much brought everything at once.  They are super friendly and professional however. Recommended.

name: Bone Daddies Old Street
address: The Bower, 211 Old St, London EC1V 9NU, UK

reviews.text: I ordered the sweet and chilli pig bones, fried chicken bao and duck bao. It was a pleasant surprise that you can order two different baos instead of having to choose the same flavour. The pig bones were absolutely amazing — I’m not even sure I’ve ever tasted anything that delicious. The sauce was rich and flavourful, and the meat was incredibly juicy and tender. Highly recommend! The atmosphere is cool and vibey, and the staff are very friendly — special shoutout to Chelsea!

Bone Daddies at Old Street is one of those places I keep coming back to when I just want proper ramen done right. No gimmicks, no overthinking. Just solid execution.

The ramen here is genuinely very good. I love the soup. Rich, comforting, and full of depth without being overly heavy. You can tell it’s been worked on properly. The noodles were cooked well too, with good bite and texture, exactly how ramen noodles should be.

The fried chicken deserves its own mention because it was sublime. Crispy, juicy, full of flavour. Honestly, it could stand on its own even without the ramen. Loved it and would happily order it again just for that.

The space itself is small, and evenings get absolutely packed. It can feel a bit chaotic during peak hours, but that’s also part of the energy. Food comes out fast, service is prompt, and everything moves efficiently despite how busy it gets.

Price-wise, it’s very affordable, especially for London. You leave full and satisfied without feeling like you’ve overpaid, which is always appreciated.

This is also a great spot for a simple, no-pressure dinner date. Casual, lively, good food, and you’re not stuck shouting across the table or waiting forever for your meal.

Overall, this place does exactly what it promises. Proper ramen, great fried chicken, fast service, and fair prices. Sometimes that’s all you really want, and this place delivers every time.

Such a lovely place with a great atmosphere. The staff were very kind, attentive, and caring, which made the experience even better.

We started with edamame and broccoli as starters. The edamame were perfect, and the broccoli surprised me in a good way! I didn’t know it would be served cold, but it was really tasty, with and without the dip.

I had the T22 as a main. For me personally, it was okay. I would rate it around a 5/10, mainly because I prefer the noodles to be cooked a bit longer. The broth, however, was very good.

I also loved the table setting. You can really feel that the concept of the restaurant is designed with the guests’ needs in mind. Overall, a pleasant visit.

We had such a lovely experience at Bone Daddies Old Street. The food was absolutely delicious, full of flavour, comforting, and clearly made with care. The atmosphere was warm, buzzing, and welcoming, making it the perfect place to relax and enjoy a meal together. What really made our visit special was the service from Ashley, our waitress, who was friendly, attentive, and genuinely kind throughout. Me and my partner actually came in on a whim after spotting it from the street, and we’re so glad we did. It turned into a memorable evening we’ll happily repeat again very soon indeed.

The Ramen Rebel: A Deep Dive into Bone Daddies, Old Street
​London’s ramen scene has exploded over the last decade, evolving from a niche curiosity into a staple of the city’s culinary identity. At the heart of this movement sits Bone Daddies, the "rock ‘n’ roll" ramen bar founded by Ross Shonhan. While the brand has expanded across the capital, the Old Street location—nestled in the tech-centric hub of East London—continues to be a flagship for those seeking bold flavors, loud music, and a dining experience that trades traditional Japanese zen for a gritty, high-energy atmosphere.
​Having recently revisited this specific branch, I’m awarding it a solid 4 out of 5 stars. Here is a comprehensive breakdown of why Bone Daddies remains a heavyweight contender in the London noodle wars, and where it still has a bit of room to grow.
​The Vibe: Rock, Grit, and Neon
​Walking into Bone Daddies Old Street is an immediate sensory shift. If you are looking for a quiet, contemplative spot to enjoy a bowl of noodles, this is not it. The playlist is unapologetically heavy—think Led Zeppelin, Thin Lizzy, and The Rolling Stones—cranked up to a volume that makes intimate secrets difficult to share but keeps the energy levels soaring.
​The aesthetic is "Tokyo dive bar meets East London industrial." Low lighting, flickering neon signs, and communal wooden tables create an environment that feels lived-in and cool. It’s the kind of place that feels just as appropriate for a first date as it does for a solo lunch or a post-work debrief with colleagues. The staff are quick, tattoos are on display, and the "no-nonsense" attitude of the brand is baked into the very walls.
​The Star of the Show: The Ramen
​The menu at Bone Daddies doesn't claim to be "authentic" in the traditional sense; instead, it focuses on being deliciously irreverent. The broths here are the result of a 20-hour simmering process, and that labor shows in the viscosity and depth of flavor.
​1. The Tonkotsu
​I started with the signature 20-Hour Pork Bone Broth. This is the litmus test for any serious ramen shop. The broth was incredibly creamy, almost coating the back of the spoon, with a deep umami hit. The chashu pork was tender, boasting a melt-in-the-mouth quality that only comes from proper slow-cooking. My only slight critique was the salt level; by the final third of the bowl, it felt a little heavy on the palate, but that is arguably the "Bone Daddies style"—bold and uncompromising.
​2. The T22
​For those who find pork too heavy, the T22 (Soy-based chicken broth) is a masterclass in balance. It features pulled chicken, cock-scratchings (crispy chicken skin), and an onion and bamboo shoot garnish. The addition of the crispy skin provides a textural contrast that elevates the dish from a simple soup to a multi-layered experience.

​3. The Vegetarian Options
​It is worth noting that Bone Daddies is exceptionally friendly to non-meat eaters. Their Mushroom Ramen is a dark, earthy powerhouse that doesn't feel like a "consolation prize" for vegetarians. It’s thick, savory, and satisfying in a way that many vegetable broths fail to be.
​Beyond the Bowl: Snacks and Sides
​You cannot visit Bone Daddies without venturing into the "Snacks" section. In many ways, the sides are just as much of a draw as the main event.
​Korean Fried Wings: These are arguably some of the best in the city. They arrive coated in a sticky, spicy, and slightly sour glaze, topped with sesame seeds. The crunch is audible across the room.
​Sweet Potato Fries with Kimchi Mayo: A cult favorite. The sweetness of the fries against the fermented funk of the kimchi mayo is a pairing made in heaven.
​Pig Bones: If you’re feeling particularly primal, the sweet-and-sour glazed pig bones are a messy, glorious delight.

It’s the perfect spot for a loud dinner with friends or a solo comfort-food mission. If you haven't been, or if it’s been a while, the Old Street branch is a reminder that when it comes to "dirty" ramen, Bone Daddies still wears the crown.

Had an amazing experience at this Japanese restaurant! 🤩 I ordered the Chicken Katsu Curry 🔥 delicious! Tender, flavorful meat and perfectly cooked rice - yum! 🍚 Miso souo were spot on too.
Calm, clean vibe, super welcoming atmosphere 😌. Staff were friendly and on point.
Highly recommend for authentic Japanese food in a great setting! 👍

Still thinking about this bowl days later.

Walked into Naniwa expecting “just sushi”… walked out questioning every other sushi spot in the UK.

The tuna don was silky, clean, and properly cut — none of that chewy supermarket energy. Rice was seasoned right. Miso actually tasted like miso, not salty water. Even the wasabi had a kick that woke me up.

Simple. Precise. No gimmicks.

If you know, you know.
If you don’t — go. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
11.99
The waiter was super friendly and funny, which makes the whole experience feels like home. The signature tuna roll (dont remember the exact name) was our favourite. Truly enjoy and tasty.

Really enjoyed my meal here. The staff couldn't be friendlier and the food was very good.

Didn't try it this time but the sushi looked very popular so will definitely be going back

Dropped in between trains and was not disappointed, seemed to be full of Japanese people which is a good sign. It's a small place so my baggage had you be put away.
I had a sushi selection which was fresh and tasty. They have tamari which is gluten free, and one of the staff showed me to add more wasabi to it.
Friendly and affordable too. Will go back, it gets busy quickly so will book next time

name: Sanjugo Shoreditch
address: 13-15 Great Eastern St, London EC2A 3EJ, UK

reviews.text: Excellent service and friendly staff. Great quality food and good variety.  They also have a good lunch deal. Comfortable seating and easy to get to. Would go back again. My friend came here for dinner one night and then took me here for lunch.  We’re both very happy. Thank you

Don't listen to any negative reviews. Just arrived in London and this place was within walking distance from our hotel. Everyone is so nice, and the food is fresh and delicious. We live in Miami & NY and have to say this place is one we would definitely return to. You feel catered to, acknowledged, and appreciated. Love the cosy & intimate vibe.

A week day first time visit to Sanjugo, we arrived slightly earlier and were were seated down. The Menus where presented and very much like coffee table books, clear and well presented. We decided and ordered our dishes and drinks. They came out quickly and the food was fine. The only comment was that my dish Chicken Katsu Curry with Rice wasnt hot as I had wished, but it was fine. Everything else was well presented and tasty and met our expectations. I would say the food was fine, but again, London has multiple eateries that offer very much the same dishes at a similar price point. If you are in the area, them drop on in and give it a try. It is close to City of London and does a lot of the City folks as well as well as the Shoreditch Tech crowd. Enjoy, a nice eating experience.

Came here for a birthday meal and it was amazing! Food was incredible and as a group of 4 we managed to try loads of different dishes for a really reasonable amount. Staff were kind and friendly and brought out a birthday dessert too! Perfect evening and highly recommend. Our favourites were the prawn miso roll, Nasu Dengaku (amazing), and marinated chilli chicken. Thank you

Turned up without booking. Wanted to try some Japanese food, never tried it and heading to Japan in a few months.

Everything was really decent, the honey chicken roll is incredible. Unagi and Tuna nigiri were good, shame there was only 2 of each! Service was superb, asked for a recommendation and went for the spicy tuna roll, preferred the honey chicken but it was still superb.

Ill come back next time I'm down in London!

I stopped by The Sushi Bar on Brick Lane for a casual Saturday night dinner and tried a few dishes:
•	Chicken Yakisoba 🍜 – Nicely prepared and cooked well, but it lacked a bit of flavour.
•	Chicken Gyoza 🥟 – Delicious, though I personally prefer them steamed or boiled rather than fried. It would be great if they offered a choice in preparation style.
•	Prawn Katsu Roll 🍤 – Pretty decent and satisfying.

Overall, it’s a good spot and worth visiting if you’re after a quick bite at a fair price. Just don’t expect deeply authentic Japanese food prepared by East Asian chefs — it’s more of a casual fusion take.

The restaurant itself is simple, clean, and tidy. When I visited, it was a quiet evening with only a couple of other tables occupied, so there wasn’t much of an atmosphere — though that might just have been the night.

A nice little stop for sushi lovers who want something quick and affordable on Brick Lane.

We looked for Chinese/asian food near our hotel that is halal. The food was delicious and also the staff and the owner are very friendly and you feel very welcomed there.
Also it was very beautiful to watch how respectful they're behaving and talking towards each other. When we come to London again, we will definitely go there again. Greetings from Germany! |

Absolutely Fantastic Dinner!
I had dinner at The Sushi Bar Brick Lane today and it was outstanding from start to finish. The food was incredibly fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavour. Every dish tasted like it was made with real care and attention. The service was just as impressive friendly, attentive, and welcoming without ever feeling rushed.
I’ll definitely be going back.
Han and my girls

⸻

A Hidden Halal Gem Near Brick Lane – Fresh, Flavourful & Family-Friendly

We had a delightful experience at this sushi bar near Brick Lane. Every single item we ordered was fresh, tasty, and beautifully presented. The crispy chicken bao buns were phenomenal, and the beef noodles were absolutely fantastic.

Service was quick — everything arrived within minutes, straight from the kitchen, piping hot and full of flavour. What really stood out was how accommodating they were with our toddler. All of the staff were super friendly and They kindly offered him multiple strawberries and mochi on the house, which was such a thoughtful touch.

This place is a true hidden halal gem, and we’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended!
I was mainly interested in having Takoyaki. I loved each item. They were fresh and tasty. I would definitely visit again to try other dishes when I am around again.

Absolutely loved the food here! Not only was everything delicious, but it was so aesthetically pleasing—perfect for photos. The sushi was fantastic, and the prawn tempura was a standout. Don’t sleep on the crispy asparagus either; the texture was spot on. Dessert was delicious too! Combined with the great service and a lovely atmosphere, this is easily a new favourite spot

Both the food and the service was exceptionally good. All the dish we had was delicious, good quality fish with some western twist, which was never too much and we could still feel home. Especially we really liked the Yellow tail collar. Thank you very much for your wonderful hospitality and I cannot wait to go back.

Booked this restaurant as there is a 2for1 promotion for ramen. We had seafood and pork belly ramen. The soup base were delicious, however, I didnt like the noodle texture. It was very doughy, and I like it to be more chewy. Matvha tiramisu was tasty and not too sweet. Medium price range for its quality givne 2for1 ramen.
