They no longer make you wear the in-house bowling shoes, which means once checked in, you can go straight to the lane.

We paid £25 per person for 2 games, which felt worth it for the quality of the lanes.

Perfect spot if you want a smooth, hassle-free game in Shoreditch

place was pretty cool however extremely loud. had a great time last night being served by Joao being both a great bar tender and small-talk-companion

Julie was a killer host with her fluffy bucket hat sorting out any and all problems that arose during my time at the book club

not sure of the man’s name but whoever was also working in kitchen was great sorting out any mistakes that arose with food, even if they were mine!

would recommend, the staff were all more than just friendly - you feel like you’re talking to a real human and not a customer service bot

security was also very present making sure to make the place both feel and look secure for its customers

in short, 10/10 experience and will recommend to friends

I used this spot to network with a potential vendor and get some work done. I love the vibe of this place. There's plenty of seating that comfortable. It's also a dynamic space too that has a good mix of play and work which I like. The food is hearty and filling at the right price. This is a great place to meet friend and socialize or get some work done. It depends on what time of the day you show up.

The vibe was nice, the venue itself is very pretty and the music was good - they also serve food up to a certain time. However, the entry fee on the day we went was £10 and a double vodka coke was £10.50, so the drinks and entry are quite standard for London. My experience with the bouncers was positive at first (although I've seen others reviewing that they were not so lucky). Later in the evening, my friend wasn't let back in even though his wrist was stamped and our girl friends were let back in - there seems to be some kind of selective entry after a certain time. There were some people in the club who were very clearly there to start a fight - kept intentionally bumping in to people and then getting angry, so the place can attract a bit of a weird crowd. Otherwise, the club in itself was pretty cool!

Very good breakfast (strictly 5!), good menu, nice place & kind service. Also suitable for big groups. The cappuccino was....far from our standard, not tasty, but the gladly gave us a refund with a smile. We find it great attitude & service.

Been here both during the day and evening. Brunch is not bad, but I’ve definitely had better, especially the bread. When I came there were quite a few things not available even though it was the start of Sunday brunch, so was a bit disappointed.

During the evening the place gets really crowded but the music is decent and the downstairs becomes a dance floor. It’s a lot cleaner and nicer than many clubs and bars in the nearby area.

I went there with a group of friends for Sunday roast. We were sat upstairs which was a welcoming and pleasant space.

The roast cam quickly after the order and we were pleasantly surprised. The portions were large and had plenty of vegetables in -the chicken roast to share in particular was a huge portion. The chicken and veggies were very well cooked. My friends said that the beef was quite tough, though.

Service was polite and helpful.

I would definitely return.

Okay guys, we need to talk seriously😆
This potato with ox cheeks is absolutely mind-blowing🤤
If I understood correctly, it’s part of the festive menu.
If you’re booking a Christmas party here you absolutely have to order this dish.
The booking manager and waitress Karyna were incredibly attentive.
The food and drinks were outstanding — thank you!
LOVE THIS PUB I hosted a charity fundraiser pub quiz here. The staff were so lovely, helpful and fun. The space upstairs (the Jago) is great for private events. Thank you so much for having us!

We were there for Christmas Day meal.  It was prefix  so it was what would be a standard Sunday roast meal.  Top 5 worst meals I’ve ever had.  Basically a pile of slop on my plate.  The vegetables were under cooked and the meat was so over covered it was barely edible (let alone cuttable).  Yorkshire pudding tasted like chemicals. It took 3.5 hrs for the complete meal!  There were probably 35 people dining in the pub.  They should stick with pouring beer and leave the cooking to the professionals.

Such a gem! Came here for a casual dinner and was really impressed. The roast beef was perfectly cooked and full of flavour. Loads of beers on tap — something for everyone’s taste. Service was quick and genuinely warm, waiter Karina was amazing . Definitely one of the best pubs in the area.

name: Diwana
address: 96 Brick Ln, Greater, Bethnal Green, London E1 6RL, UK

reviews.text: My girlfriend’s favourite cuisine is the Indian one and she is always on the lookout for some new Indian restaurant, where we have not been and the food is authentic, the ambience cozy and this is how we happened to have found this lovely spot with great lunch specials for about 7 quid!! Impressive deal and even more impressive buffet, where you can really can help yourself with some really tasty dishes! I don’t think that you can beat that! It may get a bit crammed at times, but that is quite understandable, giving the price.

I have no bad impressions regarding the service, quality of food, so as the taste and variety of dishes I have been able to have so far in Diwana. When possible, I am always trying to have my lunch in here and take advantage of the great price and generous portions you get for it! The place is not offering a high-end ambience, but I don’t think that if you are keen for Indian cuisine, such factors would matter, at least they don’t matter for me at all!

This is the best Indian restaurant in this area. The best Indian food that I ever tasted! They offer a great selection of vegetarian dishes. All are surely delicious and good to taste. Perfectly made up of healthy and fresh ingredients. Definitely a perfect spot to all vegetarian and health conscious locals. Very simply but surely feed your appetite.  Service is great as well as the ambiance. The staffs were very friendly and attentive. I loved to go back here again on my next visit.

I've been going to the Diwana since I was a kid. It was excellent 30 odd years ago, and literally nothing has changed. This is an amazing achievement for a restaurant in central London to stay this good and this reasonably priced for so long. I've been going to the Diwana about once per month for all this time, and although quality inevitably does vary (chefs change shifts, you get more or less cardamom in your Lassi), it's still always phenomenal value and usually, one of the best Indian vegetarian meals you can buy in London. The coconut chutney is wonderful, the panni puris are delicious and fun to play with, and the deluxe dosa is a reliable treat. They are also very vegan friendly and will happily make you some non-dairy coconut chutney if you ask. Obviously I'm biased as I've been going here my entire life and feel sentimental about it, but having watched so many family restaurants in London get successful, renovate, expand, then kick up the prices or lower the quality of the food - it's really impressive that this restaurant has been such a reliable and constant part of London life. That's what the fifth star is for!

It was a Sunday afternoon and we were looking to eat lunch before we hopped back on the train at Euston station and we found this place. It ticked all the boxes - cheap but good food. The place was full of customers but they quickly found us a table. The selection of food on offer for the buffet was very good - everything tasted good and seconds were a must! We left with bellies filled, satisfied and would happily come again.

We had a truly wonderful evening at Galvin La Chapelle. The food was outstanding from start to finish. Refined, beautifully executed, and clearly driven by an impressive attention to detail. Every course felt thoughtful and intentional, and the overall experience made us feel genuinely special. The elegance of the space only amplifies that feeling. It’s a stunning room and a place that clearly takes pride in excellence.

That said, there were a few moments that slightly broke the magic. We could hear the service director being very harsh with one of the waitstaff several times, right behind our table. We completely understand that a Michelin-starred level of service demands precision and high standards, but those kinds of call-outs would be far better handled discreetly or in private. Hearing it repeatedly made us uncomfortable and genuinely felt bad for the server.

In a bizarrely human and unforgettable twist to the night, we later had two waitstaff members standing behind our table and one of them let out an absolutely legendary fart. It was so unexpected that we couldn’t help but laugh hard. Maybe it was the final personal touch of the evening, certainly memorable and will live forever with us.

All things considered, we had a great night, enjoyed incredible food, first class service and would absolutely recommend the restaurant. We’d happily return and look forward to doing so again soon.

Having been long time fans of the Galvin’s food, we were so pleased when Galvin La Chapelle opened on our doorstep back in 2009.

We dined here on their opening night and have been regular guests since.

It’s been fantastic to enjoy the food here over the years, always precise, technical and tasty. Consistency and standards have remained high.

Service continues to be professional and polite and the dining room is probably my favourite in London.

Today we enjoyed the special Toast and Taste Menu. 5 courses and a drink for only £49. A bargain for Michelin starred cooking in central London.

An easy recommendation for a special lunch in lovey surroundings.

We went to Galvin La Chapelle for the  lunch tasting menu.

It was a beautiful restaurant with a warm and stylish decor. The bare ceiling made it especially interesting and a contrast to the aesthetic of the rest of the restaurant. It looks like it may have been a church.

The staff were very attentive and explained each course. The food itself was very interesting with a mixture of flavours and textures which were delightful. I would love to return to try their a la carte menu.

Overall, a very pleasant lunch.

We were given an amazing gift experience at Galvin La Chapelle for a three-course set menu with a glass of sparkling wine, and it was truly wonderful. We went for my birthday, and it made the day feel so special.

The staff were incredibly welcoming and genuinely kind from the moment we arrived. Every member of the team was exceptional. Dom and Matt were so attentive, the maître d’ was wonderfully warm, and the lady who served us dessert was absolutely lovely.

The whole meal was delightful, and we felt so well looked after throughout.
We’ll definitely be coming back.

I came here for dinner by myself.

Overall, this place has a Bailie, unique and magical ambience. The interior of an old chapel is one of the more unique and charming Settings for a restaurant that I have ever seen.

I will say that my expectations were very high, as a place has Michelin  star. Overall, the Service was very good, but not extraordinary. The food was excellent, but again – I was not as impressed with the food as I would have expected – I feel the food that I got at sketch. Two nights ago was much more, outstanding, and culinary. Perfect and unique.

Overall, I would be unlikely to return at the Price point, but it is a quality restaurant, and I do feel that it is deserving of it status.

A table for two arrived at 5:30 on Thursday and we only waited about 20 minutes.  The restaurant was packed inside but organised.

We ordered the steak rare, which was cooked to a perfect Basc medium rare. The fries were delicious and the sauce was spot on. I also highly recommend the rum cake for dessert.

The service was fantastic and incredibly fast.  The only menu item offered was steak and fries, which explains the quick turnover.

Wait wasn't too bad after 8.30pm on Saturday.
Salad was fresh with a strong mustard dressing. Our waitress forgot to bring our baguette and it was not warm when it was brought to us (without butter). Steak wasn't very hot, and second serving came shortly after first serving arrived.
Profiteroles looked good, but sold out very quickly. Probably best to order at the start of the meal.
Mont blanc was very disappointing, there was limited chestnut purée and full of cream.

This is simple french dining, dont expect it to be extraordinary. It's simple menu of salad for starter, fries as a side and two servings of meat with a nice gravy sauce. Considering the price in the location, I would say this was a decent affordable meal. So I'm happy with the food option. Dessert was also delicious! Service as you come in is lacking, I know the french are not known for customer service, but it is necessary in London? I don't know, but the waitress that actually served our food was really nice (sadly didn't get her name). Highly recommend for a dinner for two, or a small group

Went on a wet Saturday afternoon. Got there around 11.50 and was second line. By 12 maybe  about 6 or 7 couples.
Ordered one rare and 3 medium.
Got the salad which I liked but maybe put too much dressing.
Bread was nice but no butter!!!!!
We all preferred the rare which was my one and unfortunately had to share it with the rest of the family.  I seriously couldn't really taste much of the sauce that it was famous for.  Felt like it needed more flavor.  All those YouTube videos may have exaggerated the taste. This is very subjective.
Chips were great.
Service was ok. No complaints.

When we left at 1pm there was still plenty of tables.

For family of 4 and one bottled water it came to £151.33

Good experience.

Everything was excellent! We arrived at around 6pm on a weekday and were seated almost straight away. The service was very speedy and the food - from the salad and steak to the fries and chocolate cake - was excellent. We’d definitely visit again.

Came for brunch and we were not disappointed. Great menu with lots of choices. Definitely something for everyone.
Food was freshly prepared and beautifully presented.
Juices were amazing!
Staff very friendly and professional.
We had hoped to visit the secret bar but unfortunately it didn’t open till later! Maybe next time!

Had a splendid time at the Breakfast Club on Sunday! I came in with my colleagues as we had our team building event and we had the perfect morning before work!

Eleanor was amazing from the get go, she served us with professionalism and warmth. She was really sweet and provided exceptional customer service to the entire team.

The food was amazing too! I ordered the Full Monty and it was the best full English breakfast I've ever had. It was super filling and I skipped lunch for the day haha!

Thanks to Eleanor and the entire team at Breakfast Club Spitalfields, I'll definitely visit again and get as many people as I can. Highly recommend visiting!

Specifically, The Mayor of Scaredy Cat Town.
Great setup, was a surprise for my partner so she was a bit confused about the Smeg as I'm sure a lot of people are.
Service in TMoSCT was excellent, very attentive, always keeping an eye on your drinks levels.  Food was lovely too!  Really cool atmosphere.
Bottomless Brunch is decent value for money.
Highly recommend.

We had a wonderful time at The Breakfast Club in Spitalfields! My partner is lactose intolerant and they kindly offered plant based pancakes — they were absolutely delicious. We also enjoyed two creamy oat milk cappuccinos, simply perfect.

A very special thank you to Aoife, our lovely waitress💖💖. She was not only sweet and attentive, but also took the time to recommend fun activities for our trip. Her kindness truly made our experience unforgettable🥰

The staff in general were amazing — fast service, spotless place, and such a welcoming atmosphere.

Highly recommend this spot to everyone visiting London, it’s a must! 🌟

This spot is just a short walk from Liverpool Street Station, so the location is great and very central.

We had our Sunday morning breakfast here and really enjoyed it. At 8:45 there were barely any tables taken; by 10 most were full.

The selection is big enough to suit pretty much everyone. We especially appreciated the wide range of vegetarian options and found the “sausages” super tasty. Hash browns were honestly the best we’ve ever had. Pancakes were fluffy, though very filling.
The baked beans, however, weren’t to our taste – honestly, we’d even prefer the canned ones :D.. But of course, taste varies!

The staff were relatively kind. There are only two bathrooms, both plastered with stickers and little notes from strangers, which is a really fun touch. Cleanliness could be improved a bit, though.

One thing to keep in mind: there’s an “optional” 12.5% service charge added to the bill. So, in my opinion, there’s really no need to tip extra if that‘s already included (as a tourist, I always find this kind of pre-set charge a bit questionable).

The service and atmosphere was fantastic, the food was also great if chosen correctly.

On Valentines night we chose the whole roasted lobster and stuffed saddle of lamb, the lobster was perfect but the lamb was stuffed alright, stuffed with too much and hardly any lamb.

It tasted nice, but stick with the duck amd waffle. The lamb was disappointing but everything else was top notch.

We chose this restaurant to celebrate our anniversary on Sunday, and I’m so glad we did. From the moment we arrived, the service was amazing, friendly, attentive, and welcoming throughout.
The food was outstanding, and the views alone are worth every penny. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for a special occasion, I would absolutely recommend it. You’re paying not just for the food, but for the whole experience.
That said, I didn’t order an alcoholic drink because of the prices. While I understand that London is expensive and that this place reflects the quality and overall experience it offers, I do think they could consider offering more affordable drink options and focusing the higher price point on the food instead.
A lovely touch was the complimentary dessert they provided for our anniversary, it made the evening feel even more special.
Overall, we had a wonderful time, and I’m really happy I chose this restaurant to celebrate our second anniversary. It was a memorable experience.

Such a vibe being up on the 40th floor. We got super lucky and scored an absolutely perfect window seat with view of the Tower Bridge, which honestly made the whole experience for us.
Tip on seating:
We booked the "festive brunch" which was at a normal table. It seems like window seats are mostly reserved for pairs, while bigger groups usually get placed in the middle. If you're a group of more than two, try for the "counter table", there seem to be a few tables with a nice view.
​The food was good. I also tried orange wine for the first time. The waiter was so kind and took the time to explain the tropical flavor profile to me.
If you're veggie: there aren't many vegetarian options on the set menu we had, so check the à la carte if you have the option.
Overall: the service felt a little rushed at times, could be also because it was a public holiday. In my opinion, it’s worth the money if you get a window seat. Without the view, it might feel a bit "meh," but with it, it's a highlight.

We had a wonderful evening celebrating my birthday at Duck & Waffle. The food and cocktails were excellent, and the atmosphere made the night even more special. A special thanks to Sommelier Luis, who took great care of us throughout the evening. His professionalism, warm hospitality, and great recommendations truly elevated our experience. Everything about the night was delightful, and it’s definitely a place we will happily return to. Highly recommended for a memorable evening in London!

Such an incredible atmosphere and welcome. It was like being transported into another place entirely. Our waitress Tilly was so friendly, welcoming and attentive. She had a lovely chat with us while we paid and made the experience even better!

The food was unique and tasted incredible. I would definitely go back here on my next visit!

I can’t recommend the Horse and Groom highly enough for any private celebration — they truly exceeded all expectations!

I recently hosted my 50th birthday there, and the entire experience was outstanding from beginning to end. The team went out of their way to make the evening feel special and completely stress-free.

The venue itself is ideal: great location, plenty of space, warm atmosphere, and beautifully arranged for a private party. Every member of staff — from security to the bar  — were professional, friendly, and genuinely attentive, ensuring all of our guests felt welcomed and well looked after.

The vibe on the night was fantastic. The sound system is excellent, and the fact that it’s included in the room-hire price (along with fast, efficient staff and security) is a huge bonus. It all came together to create a truly unforgettable celebration.

If you’re planning an event, the Horse and Groom is an easy choice. You won’t be disappointed!

A brilliant pub with an even better team. We hosted a work quiz night upstairs in the Horse & Groom and Neil and team made everything so easy. Nothing was too much trouble in the planning and the bar staff were incredible throughout the evening - and they make a great aperol! The perfect space. If I could give 6 stars, I would!

I go to Unique Rhythm event every 3rd Saturday in the month. It is brilliant, several DJs playing soulful house music. If you want to have a good time surrounded by good people, good music and have a good dance it's the place to go.

We held a work event on the first floor with about 75 people. It was a great space and everyone had a good time. We had a DJ, the sound system and lights are great. The bar staff were friendly and efficient. We ordered pizzas which were all tasty. Recommend booking for your event.

Unique Rhythm Soulful House Parties are the best. Fantastic Djs who really get the crowd going. The music is outstanding and the atmosphere is super.
Never the same old music, always something wonderfully different. The Djs interact with the crowd and clearly love what they do.
I absolutely recommend this event, never any trouble and I always feel so safe.
BIG UP UNIQUE RHYTHM SOULFUL HOUSE PARTIES!!!!
Sheryl Powell.

Great atmosphere and amazing food! The service was fast and the portions were very satisfactory. I had the half eggs benedict and half potatoes and the pancakes with lemon cream, fruits and maple syrup. Also cappuccino was very good. Staff was very friendly and attentive! The atmosphere was calm and it was easy to talk and relax! Overall would definitely recommend and definitely will visit again!!!

Had an amazing experience here at the breakfast club. The food was AMAZING! Was honestly so impressed. The servers were fantastic, very attentive, helpful and friendly. The atmosphere was lovely and the interior of the restaurant is so cute. Would definitely recommend!

1 white americano & bean shakshuka with 2 extra eggs & chorizo £27.00  (extras - 2 x eggs £3 and Chorzo £2.50)
First time here on a Sunday monring 8.45am
The lighting isnt great inside, its particularily dark/dimly lit and in the corner where my table was located and I had to use my phone torch to read the menu. Im not sure if the lights are on dimmer swtiches but they could definatley do with turning up. The decor is also a bit drab and not very uplifitng or insipring.
I ordeed the Anvars Turkish Eggs and an Americano, though I was told a few munites later that my food order wasnt available today, so i opted instead for the Bean Shakshuka with 2 extrra eggs and chorizo.
My order arrived swiftly, yet it was cold in places and just tepid in others, so it was sent back for a replacement. Obviously microwaved from a pot but not temprature checked/probed before serving.
My replacement also arrived fairly swiftly and was this time hot, though clearly microwave hot !
I will also add the portions are not very generous. My shakshuka was served on a very shallow plate, almost like a sandwhich plate with a lip, a very thin layer of the shakshuka only just covered the surface of the place . I felt as if the toast that come with it as the accompaniment was the main feature as that dominated the plate, where it should be the other way around.
The waiting staff are very polite,attentive and helpful despite the food not being up to much.
To summerise I would say very overpriced for average food.
I dont mind paying good money for food but it has to be decent quality, served hot, and enough of it to make me feel statisfied that ive just eaten.
There are far better places localy to eat for the same or maybe even slighty less where you will find better sized portions and served piping hot. And the lights switched on !

I thought it was a good place with a good atmosphere. I thought the food was pretty good, too. I had the shakshuka, I prefer a bit more spice and usually have it without beans but it was decent. My friends really liked the vibe and the food they ordered, and one of my friends really liked the service. So although I found it to be an average brunch place with normal service, I took their input into consideration for this slightly above average rating.
Manuel swapped our table to more comfortable booth after we were served to different table which was very kind. Good service and good on Sunday afternoon, we will come back again. Thank you :)

Went for reef beef bubble January deal with my friend. The menu provided isn’t very accurate of what’s been served.
The steak is a rump steak instead of sirloin like in the menu, both steak (medium rare) and lobster are a bit of dry. I had add on giant grilled prawn which is just one medium sized prawn and bit dry as well (and less fresh)
Instead of a pint of Asahi 0.0% they only give you the bottle (330ml).
Overall average experience for the price we paid, would expect more for a nice looking place like this.

What a fab place. We took our sausage dog and her 7 favourite humans and the service was flexible, professional, warm but very unimposing. The food was delicious and liked by everyone. Drinks were of a high standard and it's a very attractive place. We all loved it thank you

I liked everything about the Cinnamon kitchen. Large atmosphere but still felt cosy. The waitresses were knowledgeable and friendly. The food was served  fresh and cooked to perfection.
The duo musicians who came late to play guitar and saxophone were also super. The only problem is that they played toooooo loud that i couldn't hear my friends voice.
I think the music was too loud for the restaurants atmosphere.
Overall i would definitely recommend Cinnamon kitchen
and I would go again. Hopefully the music is a little lower!.

Fabulous location. Absolutely stunning setting for an evening dinner with friends or a cozy couples date, or even just a drink or a cocktail. Gorgeous outdoor area with the heaters, seeds, blanket/throws, all under a beautiful atrium. Menu pretty decent and mid range. Reasonable prices. All food came out pretty good and fair price. Dog friendly. Would definitely go again as a nice place to meet up with the girls for lunch/dinner/drink drinks.

We went to Devonshire Terrace for dinner tonight and we had the unfortunate experience of seeing mice in the restaurant. The meal and environment were nice, however we saw a mouse a few feet away from our table while we were having dessert. We told a staff member about the unsanitary issue, who raised it to the manager, but no action was taken. We were not offered any compensation or apologies, and the staff member told us that other customers had a similar experience and management took no action.
As this is so unsanitary, I cannot recommend this place and hope they address the pest issue.

Took my friend here for his farewell dinner in London and we had a great meal. The sirloin steak was charred on the outside and juicy in the middle, cooked exactly right. The beef dripping chips were thick‑cut, golden and addictive, while the beef dripping fries were crisp and impossible to stop picking at. The mash with gravy was smooth, buttery and comforting, and the macaroni cheese was creamy, gooey and easily the side that stole the show. Friendly service and a relaxed atmosphere made it a really nice evening.

Wonderful, wonderful steak. Pictured is the chateaubriand, cooked medium rare and absolutely delicious - the bérnaise sauce was a wonderful addition to the gorgeous texture. Service is friendly, and the setting is also very nice.

Always a safe choice when looking for a restaurant. Hawksmoor never lets you down, and I have been to alot of them.

Finally got to try the Big Matt, was nice, but now I have tried it I won't need have another. Il stick to the steak.

Service was good on the night, real good buzz for atmosphere considering it was a Tuesday.

Reliable, but never amazing.

Food is very nice, lots of Steak and dessert choice so there is something for everyone :)

Unfortunately we had to wait a while to be seated although we had a reservation, but the waiter made up for this by giving us some free food. They also forgot that we were there for a birthday so we had to remind them which felt a bit awkward.. The lighting is also a little too dim.

We visited for a family meal in October. The cocktails, wine, food was fantastic, you'll defo leave feeling full! As a vegetarian, it can be difficult in meaty places but they still offer options. My fellow guests love coming here for steak and is one of their favourites / go to. The service was exceptional, always topping up, attentive and nothing was too long of a wait. The lady that served us even advised me what I could / couldn't eat on the table as we were having sharers and even offered alternatives they could make for me which was thoughtful. Only minor thing I'd say is I'd personally prefer ice cream with the sticky toffee pudding!

Lovely service and amazing food. Steak is always brilliant but the sides are wonderful too especially the spinach! The sundae dessert also blew me away, I thought it would be way too sweet but it was lovely (shared between two otherwise might’ve been too much)

Generally very good, lives up to the name and reputation, with nice cuts of meat cooked well. Seafood starters also nice, freshly prepared. Sides and sauces complement the meat dishes nicely and the environment is lively, typical for a City steakhouse.

A good location for a business dinner or after work with friends/colleagues.

Excellent evening with the lads. Food was excellent as always! Steaks clocked perfectly. Service was a little slow, but Eric stepped in and bossed it from then on.

Very accommodating and looked after us very well!

We took my 15 year old cousin here as he loves steak (cooking and eating) and I've had good experiences in the past at the Mayfair location.

Prices are, like many steak places, eye watering. It was a Saturday evening and the restaurant was quiet, even when we were leaving at 8pm.

I don't object to paying for good quality food and service but I must say, we got a very mixed bag with this place.

On arrival, we were seated in a nice booth at the front.. Our server was helpful and pleasant, we were offered drinks and menus immediately, and shown the customary raw meat selection.

Interestingly most of the starters are seafood based (prawn, crab, tuna) which is a problem if you have a slightly picky teenager with you. He had the bread basket to himself (which you're charged for, which in and of itself, I find astonishing). Over 30 years of going to all kinds of higher end restaurants and this is the only time I've been charged for bread other than specialised bread baskets. Last year's teenager birthday meal was The Ivy, the year before The Savoy Grill. On neither occasion did either restaurant charge for the standard, pre-meal bread. In fact, the Savoy provided a second basket for the teenager free of charge.

To start I had the prawn tempura and the other guest had the burrata. The burrata was good quality and tasty. The prawns were generous but I found the creamy sauce and batter a sickly combination. I felt in needed more citrus, sharpness.

I ordered the sirloin as my main, teen had the Australian Ribeye and the other guest has the fillet. We ordered fries, chips and green beans to accompany alongside 2 x peppercorn sauce and 1 x Stilton.

The sirloin was beautifully cooked and very tasty. As was the Fillet. However, the ribeye was underdone and the Stilton sauce tasted only of beef gravy. We sent both back. The ribeye was refunded and the Stilton sauce left unimproved and replaced with a bernaise (at our request) in the end.

On taking the ribeye away the manager (? I assume, she never introduced herself) asked if we wanted another. We said no as we were half way through out meals. She did not return to follow up or establish what the outcome of the complaint would be. And she did not apologise.

Super disappointing.

Our waiter was very good, though, and apologetic. They did provide a Birthday sundae for the teenager but we opted not to order anything further.

In the end, the ribeye had been removed from our bill, as had the sauce.

Its worth noting that this place adds a 15% service charge. I once again implore all visitors to London restaurants to ask for service charges to be removed.

Restaurants that charge £40 for their cheapest steak and £9 for each side order should not be expecting guests to plump up staff wages. We have a living wage in the UK and, whilst I continue to (and encourage others to) tip for very good service, I don't believe in the ever growing trend on foisting service charging on customers.

And 15% is ludicrous.

A disappointment in the end, especially as it was the teenager who didn't enjoy his steak and it was his birthday. Won't be returning.

We were alone in the restaurant and had to wait for drinks when the meat was already on the table (the bartender was too busy talking), and then the waiters forgot about us and didn't come over.
The meat was of good quality, but the taste was ruined by the burning due to the cooking method.

The dessert and tart-tart were delicious

name: LOUNGE BOHEMIA - by appointment
address: 1e Great Eastern St, London EC2A 3EJ, UK

reviews.text: We had a great experience at Lounge Bohemia. We had the cocktail tasting menu and the mocktail tasting menu, and both were innovative, creative and tasty! The atmosphere was very chill and cozy. The best part was the service - we had the most attentive waiter who took the time to explain each cocktail, and you could tell they loved what they did. Felt very comfortable the whole time and didn't mind the price after such good treatment! Would recommend!

Very beautiful and intimate place, with great décor. The cocktails were well crafted with good explanations, but I found them a bit expensive. The only downside is that I
could only pay by cash or bank transfer, which was a bit annoying. I’d recommend the place for a date, although I’ve had better cocktails elsewhere (a matter of taste).
I love this place! The drinks are so creative, interactive, and almost whimsical. The service was really friendly and thoughtful too. This is a very fun drinking experience. Can’t wait to go back

Best cocktail bar I've ever been to! Not only was the popcorn the best I've ever tasted in my life, but I love the fact that they continuously top your bowl up with more popcorn a very simple detail but a great addition to the service. SHOW STOPPING COCKTAILS that you could eat !!!! Priced at a reasonable price, considering all you get. A nice relaxed, understated Bohemian vibe, And due to its appointment, only nature, I feel like the relaxed atmosphere had more of a selective crowd inside, wasn't full of influencers on their phones but just people enjoying their drinks

Naturally this is all to do with taste, and in this case it didn't sit well with me, but each to their own. Scandinavian furniture and minor theatrics in serving does not warrant these steep prices, let alone excuse the meagre quality of the booze-soaked confusions that LOUNGE BOHEMIA call cocktails. Considering we were one of two tables in the entire bar, the wait time for my recommended whiskey cocktail had exceeded limits of what can be considered acceptable. Upon being served said (premixed) cocktail from a recessed Bible, I can only surmise that the wait time can be attributed to the host having chiselled the pages from the holy book in that time himself. I'll offer my thanks nevertheless, to hatted host, for helping us guide through the almost abstract menu (albeit patronisingly and in a squatted position before our table). A minor suggestion for easing the hosts' workflow that is already swamped by pompous table-side lectures, would be an attempt to concretise the menu. Enough of the whimsy. That being said, the alcoholic gummies that were served were indeed good, and thankfully didn't come with any speeches or interpretive dances. A final word of advice, it might be best for the hosts/servers to not awkwardly stare down their guests when they walk in, and say nothing. Considering their casual dress and apish squatting, it's hard to tell who is staff and who isn't, and silently gawking at new-comers is hardly welcoming. But if this is all to your taste, no judgement. Enjoy yourself.

We booked dinner at Gaucho for a celebration, and I was genuinely looking forward to it — especially as it was my first visit after many years of living in London. The food itself was good, and I’ve included photos to reflect that. Unfortunately, the service on this particular Wednesday evening didn’t our meet expectations.

We arrived at 6:30pm, and by around 7:30pm the restaurant was full and busy. What stood out was that one waitress appeared to be managing a very large number of tables on her own. She was consistently attentive, taking orders, serving drinks, and clearing plates throughout the evening.

In contrast, the managers on duty seemed less engaged with the wider dining area. Although they occasionally helped clear a table or two, there were several moments when nearby tables needed attention and guests were waiting. At one point, a manager spent considerable time with a group of regular customers but did not check in with surrounding tables, including ours. Eventually, I had to signal to request the bill. It was brought over, but there was no check‑in about how our meal had been or any closing interaction. For a bill of over £220, the lack of acknowledgement felt surprising. Before leaving, we made a point to thank the waitress who had been working so hard, and she responded warmly. However, as we exited, the front‑of‑house team were engaged in conversation and didn’t notice us leaving.

Based on this experience, I don’t plan to return, and I wouldn’t recommend this particular location to family or friends or colleagues. The food was enjoyable, but the service on this visit didn’t reflect the standard I expected. I genuinely hope the team reviews their approach to workload distribution and guest engagement, as the waitress working that evening was doing an excellent job under pressure.

We had a great experience at the restaurant. Jessica was an excellent server — very friendly, attentive, and professional. She helped us choose a bottle of wine, and her recommendation was perfect. The wine was excellent and made our evening even more enjoyable. Thank you, Jessica, for the wonderful service!

Amazing restaurant has the rump steak and prawns for starter was exceptional. Also a special mention to such an amazing waitress Rossella really made our first time here and will be back. Beautiful service and amazing food. Very very happy thanks Gaucho's

For the price point, this was a disappointing experience. On a Friday night, the restaurant felt short-staffed. The food was mediocre: all the steaks were over-seasoned, two arrived cold, and the chips were so salty they were inedible.

The wrong sides were brought to the table, and although staff said they would be removed from the bill, they still appeared at the end. The steak knives were poor quality and struggled to cut through a marinated steak that I should have been able to cut with a butter knife.

Drinks were slow to arrive every time we ordered. Service missed many basics: clearing plates, pouring wine, checking in on the table, and serving in a timely manner. Instead, staff were often seen talking among themselves.

My last visit to this Gaucho was ten years ago. I had hoped for improvement, but it was average then and remains average now. The only positives were the warm greeting on entry,the farewell and cocktails.

I cannot rave enough about this Restaurant & Bar. The staff were welcoming and got all 10 of us sorted with drinks as soon as we arrived. After approx 20 minutes we were shown to our table. Wow, what an amazingly decorated underground restaurant. Our host was Miri, who was fantastic from the first encounter until we all left. Excellent advice on starters and drinks. The starters came very quickly and everyone was impressed with both the quality and the serving size. The wine selection was very special and we choose wonderful Red that complemented the Steak perfectly.
The mains & sides were brought out and everyone was blown away by the quality of the food. The chips were really good, spinach was outrageously good and the tender stem broccoli was the same. The 400g Ribeye was one of the best Steaks I have ever had. I had the cheesecake (as suggested by Miri) & I was done. The whole experience from start to end was amazing.

name: Gaucho City of London
address: 1 Bell Inn Yard, London EC3V 0BL, UK

reviews.text:
Recently visited Gaucho City and overall had a very enjoyable experience. The restaurant has a stylish, lively atmosphere that works well for both business dinners and special occasions. The steak was cooked well and full of flavour, and the sides complemented the meal nicely.
Service was friendly and attentive, although there were moments when it felt slightly rushed. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality of the food and the setting largely justify it. A solid choice if you’re looking for a premium steakhouse in the City.

A paradise for meat lovers, serving up rich South American flavours that make every steak feel like it flew in first class. The cuts are tender, the chimichurri is addictive, and the wine selection is so good you’ll start feeling like a connoisseur even if you’re not. Stylish, bold, and dangerously delicious. 🥩🍷🔥

Ambience was absolutely lovely, service was top quality except for the gentleman on the entrance (bold headed in a tux like suit) who was quite rude because we had a hidden disability and had to use the lift. Dog friendly which is amazing, and the steak and shrimps were to die for
The food was great. I had the ribeye and my partner the fish. The atmosphere is great. The service is on top with competent and friendly staff.

We had a fantastic evening at Gaucho City. Shared a 700g Chateaubriand with my colleague, cooked perfectly medium rare and absolutely delicious. Starters and sides were excellent, and the staff were wonderfully attentive.

We came in to experience the set menu from a Virgin Experience Days voucher.
The staff were wonderful and accommodating, and very friendly. As expected for such a high-end restaurant, everything was top notch.
The restaurant was classically decorated, low-lit and felt very intimate, which is what we had hoped for.
The food itself was DELICIOUS. We enjoyed almost all of the dishes, but some were not to our taste. A fan favourite was the beef bourguignon and the chocolate mousse. The beetroot salad was the least favourite, and felt it was too niche a dish to not be able to swap out.
Aside from this, we would definitely return, but would order from the A La Carte menu, not a set menu.

5/5 would recommend

I came here with 3 other people tonight and we had a great evening. All in all, the food was delicious, the service was friendly and the ambience was lovely.

We came for the 6 course and cocktail menu, I had a pornstar mocktail which was refreshing and tasty. We had beetroot with goats cheese and walnut, and salmon with crème fraiche as an aperitif. I then had ham hock pate with coleslaw which both complemented each other very well.

For the main I had beef bourguignon with mashed potato, I also had a honey and mustard salad which did not have much honey or mustard flavour, but it was still good nonetheless. The beef itself was exquisite, it really melted in the mouth and I’d definitely recommend.

For dessert I had a chocolate mousse which was rich and very tasty. There were also scotch wafers with cream inside which were very crunchy. I then had a cup of tea to finish.

I did notice a lot of cutlery being dropped, the restaurant is big so it was rather noisy, and I noticed quite a few back of house staff walking through the restaurant area. These and the salad feedback are the main constructive points I’d raise. The staff were very friendly and the kitchen was accommodating of food preferences and menu changes.

Overall, everything was lovely, an evening to remember for sure :)

We visited for lunch and had the 5 course taster menu. The staff were impeccable from start to finish - friendly, welcoming and professional. We loved the seating and design of the restaurant; just the right amount of space between tables so you didn't feel on top of the people near to you. Acoustics were also great as I could hear my partner and not everyone else.

The pace of the meal was perfect. We did not feel rushed and food arrived promptly for the start courses but then there were slightly bigger gaps between the following courses. It was very impressive indeed.

The food - each course was as expected for a restaurant of this standard - excellent and faultless. We loved everything served and would definitely return for another meal.

We had been gifted a 6 course menu here with a cocktail.

When we arrived we were asked to wait at the bar which was ridiculously crowded, there were over 20 people here and only 6 stools and no hangers left for our coats.

We were taken to our table and everyone from there was attentive and friendly.

1st was a choice of cocktail.

2nd and 3rd course was a few slices of beetroot and a little pancake with some salmon on.

4th was an option of makeral pate and ham hock? There was an option to upgrade £3 to have bone marrow salad. We had the makeral which was nice and very fresh and the Bone marrow which was very small but tasty.

5th course was the main, which was steak and a choice of sauce. I asked for my steak rare and was recommended to go medium rare, which I did, it arrived closer to well done.  We added fries (£12) and creamed spinach (£8.5)

Dessert was yummy we had chocolate mouse and lemon posset(this was the best one). Then tea and coffee to finish.

On top of our voucher it cost us £60 with service(we also had one drink each at the bar while we wait).

Was a nice experience as a gift but I wouldn’t go back.

I was a little apprehensive after reading some of the previous reviews, but our experience here was absolutely wonderful.

This visit was a gift through a Virgin Experience Voucher, and we were genuinely impressed from start to finish.

We chose the three-course meal with a cocktail each and couldn’t resist adding a few extras.

The food was delicious especially the sticky toffee pudding which I’m still thinking about.

The service was also friendly and attentive, even with how busy it was.

Thank you to the team at London Steakhouse for a truly memorable evening!

Incredible experience from the moment I booked the space for my Galentine's event up until the moment we packed up to leave. Alex is so accommodating and the staff for the event (Jordan and Molly) were such a delight! The guests loved the space and I would absolutely return for a future event.

I visited this site for the first time to meet a friend and I was amazed at how friendly the staff were and especially considering it was a busy Friday night, the service was also excellent. Our food arrived quite quickly and was piping hot and tasted great. I really enjoyed the atmosphere at this location, you could see why it was so busy as it is such a nice location. Loved the decor, loved the different sections of the pub as well as we had a table booked in a little nook which gave us privacy and we didn't need to shout across the table. Fully recommend.

A busy London vibing pub opposite Liverpool Station, a trendy place to hangout for a quick drink,  lounges on different levels and a private one to rent on the top floor.  A great selection of beers available on the tap. Delicious smelling food you'll not be disappointed. It also hosts a nice outdoor drinking area with tables and chairs for when the weather's good

Great pub - check out the upstairs area! Dart boards and a great place to watch the match !

You can also order from your phone and have everything delivered directly to your table! Great staff - highly recommend

I had an excellent experience booking “The office bar” in the first floor. The staff were really friendly the booking process was seamless and we were allowed to play music in the sound system and dance. I couldn’t recommend more for a private function. Very reasonably priced. A big thank you !

We visited Poppies Fish & Chips and had a fantastic experience. There was a wide variety of fresh fish options, and everything we tried was absolutely delicious. The quality and flavour were truly impressive.

A special thank you to Funda Hanım for her warm hospitality and friendly attitude. She made us feel very welcome and gave us excellent recommendations, which made our visit even more enjoyable.

We were very pleased with the whole experience and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommended!

Perfect fish - my haddock was fresh, succulent, crisp batter, just the right thickness. The chips are good (not the best I’ve had), tea is hot, coke is cold, mushy peas the way it should be. Forget the curry sauce though, it’s lumpy and pretty tasteless.

Service was great. We went on a Saturday afternoon and seating was fast.

Easily the best fish and chips I’ve ever had, and it’s clear why they’ve been in business for so long. I also tried some dishes that are less popular with tourists: whitebait (similar to French fries, but made with tiny whole white fish) and cod roe (battered and deep-fried caviar). Both were something completely new to me and absolutely delicious.

Less than 10 minutes walk from Liverpool Street, Poppies manages to be both a decent counter chippy and a full table service restaurant, and it does both well.

Visited a couple of times over the years. This visit as a group of three, seated for table service. Calamari and chips for me this time, crisp coating and tender inside. A decent wedge of lemon. Baked beans and mushy peas for the table. Chips thick cut and fluffy within. Batter light and golden. Everything tasted clean from the fryer. Portions filling.

Nice cutlery and colourful plates added to our experience. And it’s not every chipper that will serve up a G&T and a glass of wine, alongside.

All in all, good chippy, quality ingredients, quick service, a bit pricey but this is in Shoreditch.

(Last visit May 2016)

This establishment lives up to its reputation as being a great fish and chip shop. We arrived on a Friday evening and were delighted they could accommodate a table for 4 for us. Food was excellent but the portions are a bit on the smaller side. They could have added a few more chips and more tartare sauce. Food was well cooked and not greasy at all. The service was quick, efficient and friendly
Great food, historical settings, excellent service.  will make it a point to eat there if I'm back in town.

Very nice steak. Had rump, not the most expensive cut, but it was done very well. Seasoning was on point, chips were great, beer was nice and the atmosphere at lunch (2 pm ) was pretty solid. Great waiter. Dunno, pretty perfect really. Only downside was that although the benches look the part, ultimately they weren't very comfortable. Top marks though.

A very tasty portion of pie and mash in an entirely unpretentious manner.
Not cheap but very good.

Very much a meat eater's paradise but then that's how they set out their stall so you can't complain at the lack of vegetarian options. Several excellent specials on the board today but get in early or they soon disappear. Desserts are very much of the school dinners type enjoyed by City gents. Prices are very reasonable for the location and associated clientele though vegetables tend to be extra unless a key part of the dish. Serving staff both friendly and entertaining.

The worst and most expensive roast beef dinner I have had, tough elastic beef, sloppy watery spinach, and god knows what they did to the roast poatoes, black brown and texture of boiled potatoes, a pint of flat warm lemonade from a big plastic bottle, the waitress kept repeating with a scowl that service was not included, I went with a friend after listening to someone famous reminisce about his childhood memories of this place, I understand that it is smack bang in the City of London and assumed that they did not like our appearance and thus the hostile reception and the terrible food. Will never return.
This review was for my experience of this joint before it's closure, my original review at the time was not published by google for some reason.

We had an absolutely fantastic experience at the Counting House Pub in London. We were a group of 6 adults and 4 very boisterous boys, and from start to finish nothing was too much trouble.

Anouska and Ellie (hope I’ve got her name right!) were incredible—so patient, welcoming, and attentive despite how lively our group was. They made us feel genuinely looked after and went above and beyond to make sure everyone was happy. The manager was just as accommodating, which really added to the whole experience.

Amazing service, lovely atmosphere, and a team that truly knows how to look after their guests. Can’t recommend them enough—we’ll definitely be back!

Fabulous end to a great mystery tour of the financial district. Yes the beer is quite expensive, but you are in the financial district so don't expect a cheap beer! The pub has an amazing history all the way back to Roman roots (and foundations!) to more recently being a bank. Wonderful charm to the place and nice friendly staff.

The Counting House were brilliant when it came to organising our staff social event. From the moment I reached out, the communication was clear, prompt, and helpful. I want to thank Tharushi in particular for helping organise our event - she was fantastic and provided lots of guidance to ease the planning (despite there being numerous changes to our booking). The event itself was very smooth, and the venue is lovely - we booked the Ledger Room and this was great for our party size (approx 30 people). The food was also great, and the atmosphere was surprisingly good for a Tuesday in early January. Overall a great experience with The Counting House, and I would definitely recommend this venue for any kind of event.

The staff where brilliant, very helpful and friendly. The room was stylish and very clean. All of the in-room extras (soaps, coffee, drinks) where of high quality and all included. The breakfast was good also with quick and friendly service. Dispite our room being on a very busy street and with the pub downstairs we could hear little to none outside noise. Definitely would stay agian.

We weren't aware this was a hotel as well as a pub but we went in on the of chance we could get breakfast here... which they can do and it's available to non residents. We had the full English breakfast and the avocado on toast. The full English had high quality items and was delicious.  The avocado was also very tasty with an addition of a pesto dressing which was well received too.

Great location on an old historic bank and helpful friendly staff.  Highly recommended for breakfast!

Had a really great time at Balls Brothers Austin Friars. Everything just worked, good vibes, great food and a relaxed but polished atmosphere that makes you want to stay longer than planned.

Big shout-out to the manager Alberto, who honestly made the experience even better. Super attentive, really knowledgeable and genuinely professional without ever feeling stiff or overbearing. He checked in at just the right moments, gave great recommendations and made us feel properly looked after.

If you’re looking for a solid spot in the City with great service and a welcoming feel, this place is a winner. Will definitely be back! 🍷👏

We hosted our work Christmas party for a group of 126 people, and it was absolutely fantastic! From the very beginning, the communication with the team was excellent—every detail was handled smoothly and efficiently.

The staff on the night were super helpful and incredibly friendly, making sure everyone felt welcome and taken care of. The three-course meal was delicious, with plenty of compliments from our team about the quality of the food.

They were also extremely accommodating when our live band arrived to set up. The space worked perfectly for both the seated dinner and the band’s performance, creating a great atmosphere for the evening.

I can’t recommend Austin Friars Balls Brothers enough for any large event or party. A huge thank you to the team for helping us create such a memorable night!

Incredible. Had my hen party here and it was so good. The food isn’t what you go there for so I get it’s not the best quality. But the vibes, fun and party make up for it! So so good highly recommend for fun with your besties!!

Great pub, serving great food with a great service.

The venue looked fantastic and I was hosted my Flo and Alberto who looked after us with a great service, constantly smiling and making sure we had a wonderful time. Food was also incredible. Thank you to the whole team.
Great pub! Flo did a great job to bring the place back to life with a strong team. I have been there a couple of times for different occasions and I will def be back!

Hands down the greatest pub experience in LDN (and beyond). I want you to imagine the greatest conceivable buzz with the tastiest sandwiches and Portuguese plates you’ve ever had. To share with your friends. I cannot believe how good The Macbeth is — this is everything I want from a Saturday evening!

The Prego and Bifana sandwiches are famed for a reason and do not disappoint. We also shared the pink firs in aioli, fried mussels, Peri chicken and lamb Vindaloo. All ridiculously good. The Macbeth delivers both a fantastic vibe and out-of-this-world food; I am so excited to come back and explore the menu again, which changes daily. Unbelievable spot. 10/10!!

Had a really really good Sunday lunch here. Bit noisy at the front of the pub but we got seated near the kitchen area and it was quieter. The food was great, lovely staff and a nice carafe of house red  🍷 … sadly they had run out of a few things by 4.30 but we got almost everything we wanted… ( no cheesy leeks !) 10/10

If you are after Portuguese style cuisine and a good wine and beer selection then this is the place to go. Our favorite was the bifana   sandwich and the salted cod served on shoe string fries with soft boiled egg, honestly can’t wait to go back. The orange wine also paired nicely with the mussels and we had the flan for desert.
Unreal food and service. The New Years set menu was one of our favourite dining experiences of the year. Stoked this is our local in the heart of Hoxton!

Went with a friend for their opening night. There was an excited buzz in the place and a touch of nervousness to get everything right. They did. In spades. The atmosphere of the original has been kept but the food coming out the kitchen is a wonderful trip to Portugal. Small plates, incredible Bifana (MUST ORDER) and delicious seafood were finished off by a perfect slice of flan. Go now before they are too busy to get a booking at.

Went to see Lizzie Esau live. It's a little hard to find at first. Plenty of space both inside and outside. Prices were reasonable for drinks. Easy access to the bars and the performance space. Sound quality was good and as it's a small venue, a good view is fairly ready to find. Would definitely go again. Only downside for me was that to get back to Paddington afterwards isn't the easiest of trips.

I enjoyed seeing Mint Field and a little bit of Avishag Cohen Rodrigues here last Sunday. It's worth knowing that there's no cloakroom at the venue (it is only a bar after all), but the helpful staff managed to look after my coat and backpack between them during the gig, which was very much appreciated. Would happily come here again.

Great bar with live music room and a huge outdoor patio. I used to come here 15 years ago and it has not lost its character. Not sure about the service as they didn't acknowledge me for a while so I decide to check out live music without the drink and then left.

The food is tasty, the service is fair enough. On the weekends it is very very crowded and loud so the staff is doing their best to manage that crowd. I do definitely recommend to book if you are a larger group. The garden ares is such lovely with all the lights and if you book in advance you can get a table under the tent where you can stay safe in the rain

Great pub with outside space. Ideally have a reservation on saturdays to make sure you get inside but usually its not too crowded on saturdays. They have a really good cider on tap (my fav) not too sweet, not too dry. They also have food but not really gf options as far as I remember besides crisps. They have loads of outside space and heaters too! They also have three bars - one outside and two inside - top and bottom!

What an experience. We went there for a taster menu and it was good. When I say good, I mean Really GOOD!
I was sceptical about portion sizes at first, however, they proved me wrong - portion sizes were just right and the main thing is - It was mouth watering.
The staff was very attentive, polite and friendly. The atmosphere was calm, with gentle music in the background and dimmed lights.
Would definitely repeat the whole experience.
Recommended.

First visit for a company due and we had a beautiful experience at this venue in December 24. It was booked it for my colleagues many times before and every time I received exceptional feedback. The booking process and customer service were always flawless,  so I already had a positive impression that it would not disappoint the expectations. And in fact,  the venue is very beautiful,  with wonderful decor, great art pieces, and a warm atmosphere. Everything is super cozy. Furthermore, the food was delicious, and the wine choice was just great!  The only thing the lift 🛗 is slow and we stuck on the way down. Looking forward to my next visit here!!
I recommend

Lovely private member’s club in Moorgate. Beautiful decor, traditional, corporate vibe. Has a beautiful roof terrace. Also has a gym and restaurant. Gym seems well equipped, small steam room and they run boxing classes etc there.

Decidedly average tasting menu, everything was well presented but not exciting or interesting. Not a single worthy dish. Service was quite slow and even with a Groupon voucher it wasn't worth the price. Overall pretty subpar. Wouldn't possibly ever want to go again.

I cannot recommend Eight Club Moorgate highly enough, and I especially want to recognise Esther from the team for her outstanding service. From the moment I reached out early in the morning with last-minute requests for breakfast and lunch arrangements, Esther handled everything flawlessly and with a smile. She delivered on the spot, ensuring our meeting ran smoothly and our guests were completely comfortable.

My partners were 100% happy with the experience, and that was entirely down to Esther’s professionalism, efficiency, and genuine care. She went above and beyond, and I honestly can’t thank her enough. If you’re planning an event or meeting at Eight Club, you’ll be in excellent hands with Esther. She is a true credit to the club!

name: The Star of Bethnal Green
address: 359 Bethnal Grn Rd, London E2 6LG, UK

reviews.text:
I celebrated my birthday in the karaoke which was half price because it's January. We were 20 people vibing, it was great to find music in Spanish as well, which is not the norm. The staff helped me with napkins, lighter, and knife for my cake.
Pizza was very good, non alcoholic options available, decent prices for all.
After karaoke was over, we went downstairs and had the best time with the best DJ in London. He really read the room and played absolute BANGERS.

100% will be back!

So arrived here last night around 11pm. 2 door staff just standing to the side of the entrance. I proceeded to walk in and then was summoned back outside. I said 'is there a problem?' The lady door person said 'well I am just seeing how much you've had to drink...'. I said 'well clearly not enough,  otherwise I wouldn't be here' (jovial of course). She said 'well I am just looking at the confidence, the way you walked in, you have too much confidence'. I said ' well I think at the age of 49 I should have plenty of confidence by now'. She said 'no sorry not tonight' meaning I wasn't be allowed entry. I said ' OK fine' and walked to another pub. I had already had a drink, but was clearly NOT drunk. I am not a child, I am almost 50 years if age, with my best mate who is 55. We are not kids out for a fight, just an honest drink. Is it your door policy to ask people to get down on their knees and beg to get in, rather than walk straight in the door of the pub, with 'confidence ' like you would expect your customers to have? After all the door staff were not blocking the door vetting people, they were merely standing by the side of thw door allowed people to walk in unchallenged. A very bizarre reaction from your doorstaff and certainly not warranted,  especially considering that it is Christmas party time.

Lovely night for the battle of the brewery event. The general service by Dasian on the bar was brilliant and the Manager , Archie was great when dealing with the tasters from each brewer too. Overall a very enjoyable night and full of great drinks and vibes all around

A good East London boozer with warm and friendly staff, and some great burgers.
A good choice of beers, including local craft breweries. I did not stay for any events, but I bet it is.lots of fun in the evenings.
For me it was a nice quiet spot for a drink on a Saturday lunchtime, away for the bustle of Bethnal Green Road

George and DeShaun were on the bar on a Monday night and they were lovely. Never been to the bar before but they had that je ne sais quoi that means I will bring my work team here at every opportunity. What a lovely duo.

Beautifully decorated with a sleek, modern design and a clean, open view of the bar area. The service was attentive and friendly, which made the experience pleasant. We tried a few starters, honestly, they were underwhelming, so I’d suggest going for the larger plates, which might be their stronger point. Prices are reasonable for the setting, and overall it’s worth a visit.

The Anthologist is one of those rare places that strikes the perfect balance between atmosphere, flavor, and hospitality. From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed by a warm, stylish setting that feels both relaxed and refined — the kind of place that works equally well for a casual lunch, after-work drinks, or a special dinner.

The menu is creative without being pretentious. Every dish feels thoughtfully crafted — fresh ingredients, bold flavors, and beautiful presentation. The small plates are ideal for sharing (the [insert a dish you liked, e.g., Korean-fried cauliflower or truffle mac & cheese] was a standout), and the cocktails are exceptional — well-balanced, inventive, and beautifully served.

Service is another strong point. The staff are friendly, attentive, and genuinely passionate about what they do. They’re always happy to offer recommendations, which makes the experience feel personal rather than formulaic.

Whether you’re there for brunch, cocktails, or dinner, The Anthologist delivers every time. It’s stylish but not stuffy, vibrant but comfortable — a perfect spot to unwind and enjoy great food and good company.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly recommended.

Utter abomination of a meal. For £56!!! They’re laughing at us. Beetroot smoked salmon? Two wisps of it, only really detected with a magnifying glass. Crayfish salad? Invisible sea-monkeys more like. Ok soggy bread to boot.’and how about ice cold roast turkey with a shivering no-bacon pig in blanket, and gravy as watery as water. Under-cooked parsnips. The cheesecake was kind of ok. Music so loud you can’t hear the person next to you shout and service so slow our first drinks arrived way after the first course had been served. Utterly shocking. This place should be ashamed of themselves.

Excellent venue with a great vibe. I met a friend here for midweek drinks and small plates, and it did not disappoint. The atmosphere was lively, the service attentive, and we even received a great wine recommendation.

The food was outstanding, and we’ll definitely be returning. I love the bar and dining area, and even the toilets were impressive! The décor and lighting throughout are beautiful, making it a perfect spot for a date night too.

We had a dinner and a group get together after that with around 50 people. We enjoyed the food. I forgot her name but a Romanian waiter helped to our table, she is very friendly and attentive.
I also liked the decor, it was very on point with the holiday season.

Casual, lots of seating, fast service and decent food. We’ve eaten here twice this weekend for breakfast. Sunday was definitely busier than Saturday but there was still plenty of seating. No need to book, but it’s noisy. There is also outdoor seating. Family friendly the menu suits most people and there’s vegetation options. Shubui tea is great quality as was the coffee.

been here a few times and always impressed with the quality of the food/drinks. came here for a set menu christmas dinner with work and everyone really enjoyed themselves, portions were massive and definitely worth the set price.

a very large space with plenty of seating and a nicer area with sofas as well, always friendly service
What a fabulous place. Been meaning to visit for a while and finally had the chance to today. Was not disappointed. Fab aesthetic, great food and amazing staff. Will definitely be back.

A must-visit for motorbike enthusiasts! We finally made it there and were absolutely thrilled. The restaurant was great, the service very polite and friendly, and the atmosphere simply lovely. Awesome shop and, of course, the highlight was the bikes ;)

Part motorcycle clubhouse, part restaurant, and fully “moto culture,” Bike Shed Moto Co. nails the hangout vibe without skimping on the food. I came for the bikes and stayed for the steak—cooked properly, well-seasoned, and genuinely satisfying, not just an afterthought to the décor. The space is lined with beautiful machines and feels purpose-built for meets and ride-outs; even if you don’t ride, you get the atmosphere straight away. Service is relaxed but attentive, the soundtrack fits, and the room hums without being too loud for a proper conversation.

Expect a crowd on weekends and evenings; arriving early or booking ahead is wise. It’s an easy walk from Old Street, and there’s plenty to keep you lingering—bikes to admire, good coffee at the bar, and a menu that goes beyond pub standards. Prices are what you’d expect for central London and the concept, but the quality and setting make it feel worth it. A strong recommendation whether you’re a rider looking for a friendly base or just want a solid meal in a venue with serious character.

🚇Old Street
🍺 £6.80 Level Head

The Windmill is located on a quiet side street just off City Road in Shoreditch, East London. The nearest Tube is Old Street.

Originally built in the late 1800s, the pub you see today was constructed in 1869. The pub has recently undergone significant restoration and renovation, completed in 2022.

This is a good-sized, traditional one-bar pub with a few modern touches. The servery is horseshoe-shaped and centrally located, with the bar area wrapping around it. To the right of the bar is an open kitchen.

The decor consists of a boarded floor, a mix of seating, green wall panelling, and some vintage signage, but my favourite feature is the leaded stained glass windows.

The beer selection is all keg, with a lineup of well-known, familiar brands. I decided on a Level Head IPA; my pint was great, though the price point was a tad high. The food offering is traditional Roman-style pizza, with 15 options to choose from. A Margherita costs £11.

I arrived around 3:30pm on an overcast Thursday afternoon in October. The pub was quiet on arrival but soon started filling up with office workers from the surrounding area. The service was pleasant; the team member on duty was warm, welcoming, and courteous.

I enjoyed my visit here — my pint hit the spot. I loved the heritage of the building; the pizza receives good reviews, and those windows were great. Worth a look if you’re in the area

📅 16th October 2025

I went for lunch with some friends of mine. The owner accomodated us quickly, even if without reserved table. The pizza was the best I have had (potatos, tomato and sausages). The owner offere us a thinner bread/pizza with oregano as a started. The wait for food and drinks was minimum and spot on! I would teccomend the place for quality of food and incredibly friendly people. In few moments, we became friends of some regular customers. All the athmosphere is magnificent and you forget the stress of the city. The prices were incredibly low for the area. Unforgettable experience. It was my first time in this place, but I am planning to stop more often with my colleagues and friends.

Lovely pub! We popped in on a Saturday night before dinner and I only wish there’d been a few more people around! It deserves to have more costumers. The guy behind the bar was really friendly and shared some great beer recommendations.
Traditional British pub with fine beers and true Italian cuisine. We’ve tried a tasty Roman pizza (pinsa) with ham and tomatoes.
Reasonably priced food and drink, pizza here is genuinely one of the best ive had can tell its quality ingredients - £11 for a margarita in the city is very good value

I had the pleasure of photographing a beautiful wedding at Merchant Taylors’ Hall this year, and the entire experience was exceptional. The venue itself is truly stunning — full of history, warmth and atmosphere — it feels like stepping into a fairytale.

The staff were outstanding throughout the day. I especially want to highlight Donique, who looked after the couple and coordinated the timings seamlessly. The catering was also excellent, and the service was thoughtful and attentive from start to finish.

I can’t recommend Merchant Taylors’ Hall enough as a wedding venue — it’s a truly magical place to celebrate love, with a team who genuinely care about creating a perfect day.
Beautiful historic place in central London. Nearest station is Bank. Great place to host conferences like the one I attended'Livery Climate Conference'

As a wedding photographer, Merchant Taylors’ Hall is hands down one of my favourite venues to shoot at. It’s such a stunning and elegant place—every room is filled with character and charm, and there are beautiful backdrops everywhere you look. It’s honestly a dream location for capturing those timeless, romantic moments.

Guests are always wowed by the atmosphere too. There’s so much space to celebrate, mingle, and enjoy the day in style. And the team at Merchant Taylors’—especially Mohamed—is fantastic. They’re super friendly, professional, and always go above and beyond to make sure everything runs smoothly.

It’s definitely one of those venues I always look forward to going back to.

Best Regards
Doville Gail Photography

Merchant Taylors' Hall offers a unique blend of historic grandeur and modern amenities in the heart of London. Its stunning Great Hall, beautiful courtyard garden, and variety of elegant rooms make it a popular choice for events. Visitors often praise the impeccable service and delicious catering, making it a memorable experience.
Great food and great service. Such a beautiful building!!

Alright hear me now, I was influenced to go and try the £15 Friday smash burger deal at 1 Lombard street. I went with high hopes and my friend Olivia. This was a unique experience because this is the real life evidence of looks can be deceiving because the restaurant looks lovely inside, the food looks great but it all went very left very quickly.

We started of the meal having Oysters, now I’ve never tried oysters before so Olivia got them and I tried one and that’s when it all went sideways,  because I severely regret trying it them. They were watery, the texture was truly horrible and the lemon and Tabasco sauce did absolutely nothing for me. I can say it was the single worst thing I’ve eaten in my life. That was just the start to this chaotic culinary experience.

After quite a long wait the star of the show arrived the double party smashed burger with added burger for an extra £3 and a coke on the side for about £4.50. BUT did I get my coke ? No, I did not I thought maybe the waiter forgot so I reminded him and asked for some sauce to go with my chips he came back 5 minutes later with ketchup and what I hope was mayo but looked a lot like butter. The chips were good I will give them that, salty, crispy and fluffy can’t go wrong. The burger on the other hand wasn’t, it was purely texture and cheese because the patties didn’t taste of anything, the sauce didn’t add much because it was overpowered by the cheese, the pickles were lost in the burger and the bacon had no crisp and was chewy so I paid an extra £3 for weatherspoons quality bacon. Not only was all the moisture sucked out of my mouth  from the burger I didn’t have any water left to alleviate that as they would pour some in my glass and take the jug away with them and my coke, it  never arrived.

The coke wasn’t added to the bill which I don’t know how to feel about it but anyway if I was to give a recommendation after that experience I would say don’t bother, use your money else where and although it’s nice in there, lovely aesthetic but you could probably get better food and service elsewhere.
Our table enjoyed a lovely afternoon. Rodrigo was an excellent waiter, he looked after us very well. The rest of the team were great too. What a lovely find, we’ll definitely be back. Thank you!!

Upon entering I really liked the decor and how bright it was. We was seen straight away and then made our way to our table where drinks were flowing as we got the bottomless drinks for £20 each which was really nice.

We had Oysters for the starter and my partner wasn't the biggest fan as they are quite big. Tasty and was more for me lool.

For our mains, I decided to get the roast chicken and mrs got the beef which I wish I got after tasting it and was so good. The chicken was a lil dry but adding the gravy made it a lot better.

I would highly recommend if you want a nice date lunch or dinner.

Really good service and polite staff.

10/10

Brunch is very punctual, with doors opening bang on 12pm and finishing at 2pm. Service is a bit slow for such a strict two-hour slot, so the time doesn’t quite feel long enough.

However, we had a very lovely time. The atmosphere is enjoyable and the food is standard, nothing particularly stood out.

Service is friendly and professional.

we visited specifically for a roast. The staff were friendly and attentive throughout our meal.

The roast was delicious, but for a table of three we were given only a small shared portion of vegetables and cauliflower cheese, which was a bit disappointing. Individual servings would have made the experience feel more generous and balanced.

Aside from that, it was a lovely visit — stunning interior, warm service, and a truly tasty roast.
